This name is directly analogous to boundary velocity names for lighter impurities such as [carbon](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), [argon](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_argon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), and [neon](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary). Where poloidally resolved measurements are available, the local counterpart [toroidal iron velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_iron_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) provides additional information on poloidal asymmetries not captured by the flux-surface average.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the iron ion velocity is directed in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged toroidal component of the neon ion velocity at the plasma boundary, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame where phi is the toroidal angle.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal flux-surface-averaged neon velocity at the plasma boundary is the average, on the last closed flux surface, of the toroidal component of the neon ion flow velocity. The toroidal component is taken along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For a flux surface $S(\psi_b)$ at the boundary poloidal flux $\psi_b$, the flux-surface average is commonly defined by the surface-weighted limit from closed flux surfaces:

$$
\langle v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}} \rangle_{\psi_b} = \frac{\int_{S(\psi_b)} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}} \, dA / |\nabla\psi|}{\int_{S(\psi_b)} dA / |\nabla\psi|}
$$

where $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the local toroidal neon ion velocity in $\mathrm{m.s^{-1}}$, $dA$ is a surface-area element in $\mathrm{m^2}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux in Wb, and $|\nabla\psi|$ is the magnitude of its spatial gradient in $\mathrm{Wb.m^{-1}}$.

In practice this quantity is inferred from impurity spectroscopy, such as Doppler shifts of neon emission or charge-exchange lines, combined with viewing-geometry corrections and an equilibrium mapping to the plasma boundary. When direct coverage of the full surface is unavailable, the average may be reconstructed from localized measurements with assumptions about toroidal symmetry, poloidal variation, and the relevant neon charge-state population. The same concept is analogous to species-resolved boundary toroidal velocities for deuterium and nitrogen.

Typical separatrix impurity toroidal-flow magnitudes are about $10^3$-$5 \times 10^4\ \mathrm{m.s^{-1}}$, with values near zero possible in weakly rotating plasmas and larger magnitudes in strongly driven or highly asymmetric edge conditions.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the flux-surface-averaged neon ion flow is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_oxygen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged toroidal bulk flow velocity of oxygen ions evaluated at the plasma boundary (last closed flux surface).
NAMES.long:
The flux-surface-averaged toroidal velocity of oxygen ions at the plasma boundary quantifies the net toroidal bulk flow of oxygen impurities along the last closed flux surface (separatrix), collapsing the poloidal variation into a single representative scalar for the toroidal rotation state of oxygen at the plasma edge.

The flux-surface average is defined as a poloidal-contour integral weighted by the inverse of the poloidal magnetic field magnitude $B_p$:

$$
\langle v_{\phi,\mathrm{O}} \rangle = \frac{\oint v_{\phi,\mathrm{O}} \, dl / B_p}{\oint dl / B_p}
$$

where $v_{\phi,\mathrm{O}}$ is the local toroidal oxygen ion velocity at poloidal arc-length position $l$ along the flux contour.

Oxygen toroidal rotation is measured by charge exchange recombination spectroscopy (CXRS) using the Doppler shift of oxygen emission lines; combining measurements at multiple poloidal locations allows construction of the flux-surface average. The non-averaged local boundary value is given by [toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), while analogous flux-surface-averaged toroidal velocities for other impurity species are given by [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), and [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_tungsten_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_tungsten_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).

Typical edge toroidal velocities for light impurities such as oxygen range from approximately $-2 \times 10^4$ to $+2 \times 10^4$ m/s, with sign and magnitude depending on plasma current direction, auxiliary heating power, and confinement mode.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the oxygen ion bulk flow is directed in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_tungsten_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged toroidal component of the tungsten impurity ion bulk flow velocity evaluated at the plasma boundary (last closed flux surface / separatrix).
NAMES.long:
The flux-surface-averaged toroidal velocity of tungsten ions at the plasma boundary quantifies the mean toroidal rotation of the tungsten impurity species on the last closed flux surface, averaging out poloidal asymmetries that arise from neoclassical effects and centrifugal trapping. It differs from the local [toroidal tungsten velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) by applying the flux-surface average operator, yielding a single representative scalar per flux surface rather than a position-dependent field along the separatrix.

The flux-surface-averaged toroidal velocity is defined as:

$$
\langle v_\phi \rangle = \frac{\oint v_\phi \, dl / B_p}{\oint dl / B_p}
$$

where $v_\phi$ is the local toroidal component of the tungsten ion bulk flow, $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic field magnitude, and the line integral runs along the plasma boundary flux surface in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Tungsten boundary rotation is primarily inferred from charge exchange recombination spectroscopy (CXRS) using Doppler-shifted tungsten emission lines; local velocity measurements at multiple poloidal positions are then combined with magnetic geometry to evaluate the flux-surface average. The same averaging convention is applied consistently across impurity species, as in [toroidal flux-surface-averaged carbon velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) and [toroidal flux-surface-averaged neon velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary). Typical boundary toroidal impurity rotation magnitudes range from $10^3$ to $10^5$ m/s depending on heating power and toroidal momentum injection.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the tungsten ion bulk flow is directed in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_xenon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged toroidal component of xenon ion bulk flow velocity at the plasma boundary (last closed flux surface).
NAMES.long:
The flux-surface-averaged toroidal xenon velocity at the plasma boundary quantifies the mean azimuthal flow of xenon impurity ions around the torus, averaged along the last closed flux surface (separatrix). Xenon ($Z=54$) is a heavy noble-gas impurity used in radiative-mantle experiments to spread divertor heat loads, and its toroidal rotation reflects momentum balance between collisional coupling to the bulk plasma, neoclassical forces, and external toroidal momentum input.

The flux-surface average of the toroidal velocity component $v_\phi^\mathrm{Xe}$ is defined as:

$$
\langle v_\phi^\mathrm{Xe} \rangle = \frac{\oint v_\phi^\mathrm{Xe} \, B_p^{-1} \, dl}{\oint B_p^{-1} \, dl}
$$

where $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic field magnitude and the line integrals are taken along the plasma boundary contour.

Toroidal impurity velocities at the separatrix are measured primarily by charge exchange recombination spectroscopy (CXRS), resolving Doppler shifts from charge exchange between injected neutral beam atoms and Xe ions; a poloidally distributed array of sightlines is necessary to reconstruct the flux-surface average. The non-averaged counterpart is given by [toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), while analogous averaged quantities for lighter seeding species include [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) and [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_argon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_argon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the xenon ion flow is directed in the sense of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_pedestal
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the bulk helium-3 ion flow velocity at the H-mode pressure pedestal, resolved along the toroidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal helium-3 velocity at the pedestal is the component of the bulk flow velocity of $^3\mathrm{He}$ ions along the toroidal basis direction at the H-mode pressure pedestal. The pedestal denotes the steep-gradient edge region just inside the last-closed flux surface, where flows strongly affect radial electric field balance, impurity and isotope transport, and edge stability.

The toroidal component is the projection of the helium-3 bulk velocity onto the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame:

$$
v_{\phi,^3\mathrm{He}} = \mathbf{v}_{^3\mathrm{He}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the bulk helium-3 ion flow velocity and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

In practice this quantity is inferred from charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy, passive spectroscopy when applicable, or edge-plasma modeling constrained by diagnostics. The pedestal value is obtained by evaluating the reconstructed helium-3 toroidal flow at the pedestal location, commonly identified from the steep-gradient region of pressure, density, or temperature.

Typical pedestal toroidal ion velocities range from about $-1\times10^5$ to $1\times10^5$ m.s^-1 in tokamak H-mode plasmas, with isotope-specific values depending on neutral-beam momentum input, collisional coupling, radial electric field shear, and edge rotation damping.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the helium-3 bulk flow is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the helium-3 ion bulk flow velocity at the plasma boundary, resolved along the phi direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame. It characterizes rotation or flow of helium-3 ions where closed magnetic flux surfaces meet the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal helium-3 velocity at the plasma boundary is the toroidal component of the bulk flow velocity of $^3\mathrm{He}$ ions evaluated on the last closed flux surface. It describes the directed motion of the helium-3 ion population around the torus at the interface between confined plasma and the open-field-line scrape-off layer.

The component is defined by projecting the helium-3 ion bulk velocity onto the toroidal basis direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame:

$$
v_{\phi,^3\mathrm{He}} = \mathbf{v}_{^3\mathrm{He}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the helium-3 ion bulk velocity and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

In practice, this quantity may be inferred from Doppler shifts of helium spectral lines, charge-exchange measurements when suitable active neutrals are available, or from edge plasma modeling constrained by spectroscopy and equilibrium reconstruction. The boundary value is obtained by evaluating or interpolating the helium-3 flow to the last closed flux surface.

Typical boundary values are often in the range $-5 \times 10^4$ to $5 \times 10^4$ m.s^-1, with larger magnitudes approaching $1 \times 10^5$ m.s^-1 possible when strong momentum input, edge electric fields, or ion-temperature-gradient-driven flows are present.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the helium-3 ion bulk flow is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_helium_4_velocity_at_pedestal
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the helium-4 ion fluid velocity evaluated at the H-mode pressure pedestal, resolved along the direction of increasing toroidal angle.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal helium-4 velocity at the pedestal is the projection of the bulk helium-4 ($^4$He) ion fluid velocity onto the toroidal direction $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, evaluated at the H-mode pressure pedestal. This quantity characterizes the toroidal rotation of $^4$He ions within the steep-gradient edge transport barrier that governs H-mode energy confinement.

The defining relation is

$$
v_\phi^{\,^4\text{He}} = \mathbf{v}_{^4\text{He}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{^4\text{He}}$ is the local helium-4 ion fluid velocity and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

Pedestal ion toroidal velocities are measured by charge exchange recombination spectroscopy (CXRS), which resolves the Doppler shift of emission lines from $^4$He ions excited during charge exchange with beam neutrals; the pedestal value is extracted by fitting the measured radial profile and evaluating it at the pedestal location identified from electron pressure or density measurements.

Ion toroidal rotation at the H-mode pedestal spans from a few km/s to tens of km/s depending on neutral beam torque input, intrinsic rotation, and impurity–main-ion momentum coupling. The helium-4 velocity closely follows the deuterium main-ion rotation — compare [toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_pedestal](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_pedestal). The isotopic companion [toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_pedestal](name:toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_pedestal) characterizes the lighter $^3$He species at the same location, while [toroidal_helium_4_velocity_at_magnetic_axis](name:toroidal_helium_4_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) and [toroidal_helium_4_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_helium_4_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) track the same species at other radial positions.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the helium-4 ion flow is directed along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ (counter-clockwise when viewed from above in the $+\hat{Z}$ direction).

NAMES.name: toroidal_helium_4_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short: Toroidal velocity of helium-4 ions at the plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal helium-4 velocity at the plasma boundary is the local toroidal component of the helium-4 ion bulk flow evaluated on the last closed flux surface. It is a local boundary value at the evaluation point, not a flux-surface average; by contrast, [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_helium_3_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) represents a boundary value averaged over a flux surface for helium-3.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the quantity is the projection of the helium-4 bulk velocity onto the toroidal basis direction:

$$
v_{\phi,{}^{4}\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x}_b) = \mathbf{u}_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x}_b) \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the plasma boundary, $\mathbf{u}_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He}}$ is the helium-4 ion bulk velocity in m.s^-1, $\hat{\phi}$ is the dimensionless unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle, and $v_{\phi,{}^{4}\mathrm{He}}$ is in m.s^-1.

In practice this velocity is obtained from local edge ion-flow measurements, such as Doppler shifts of helium emission where available, or from edge plasma modeling and interpolation to the last closed flux surface. The value may vary around the boundary, so it should not be interpreted as a flux-surface-averaged toroidal flow unless that averaging is explicitly part of the named quantity.

Typical edge helium-ion toroidal velocities are often of order 10^3-10^5 m.s^-1, with values near 0 possible at flow reversal or stagnation points. The magnitude and sign depend on momentum input, collisional coupling to other ion species, neoclassical effects, and edge electric fields.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the helium-4 ion bulk flow is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_pedestal
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short: Local toroidal component of the hydrogen ion fluid velocity at the pedestal reference location, not a pedestal-region average, resolved along increasing toroidal angle phi in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame where R is major radius and Z is vertical height.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal hydrogen velocity at the pedestal is the scalar toroidal component of the hydrogen ion fluid velocity evaluated at a single local pedestal reference location. That reference location is set by the pedestal characterization used for the discharge, for example a fitted pedestal-top point or another declared point within the steep-gradient pedestal, so this quantity is not an average over the whole pedestal region. Comparisons with [toroidal deuterium velocity at the pedestal](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_pedestal) and [toroidal nitrogen velocity at the pedestal](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_pedestal) should use the same local pedestal reference location.

The projection onto the toroidal basis direction is

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{H}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{H}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $v_{\phi,\mathrm{H}}$ is the toroidal hydrogen velocity in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the hydrogen ion fluid velocity in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with $R$ the major radius, $\phi$ increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ the vertical height.

The local value is obtained by evaluating a measured or modeled hydrogen flow at the chosen pedestal reference location. Experimental determinations generally use Doppler-shift information from hydrogen emission or other edge-flow constraints together with viewing geometry and magnetic-equilibrium geometry; modeling obtains the quantity from the hydrogen species momentum balance and samples the same pedestal point. The companion [hydrogen density at the pedestal](name:hydrogen_density_at_pedestal) is often needed to interpret the corresponding hydrogen momentum density and particle flow.

Typical pedestal hydrogen toroidal velocities are signed and strongly scenario dependent: weakly rotating edges may be close to 0 m.s^-1, while rotating pedestal plasmas often have magnitudes of order 10^3-10^4 m.s^-1 and can be larger under strong momentum input. The value should be compared across species only when the same pedestal reference location and the same right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame are used.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the hydrogen ion fluid velocity has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short: Local toroidal component of the hydrogen species bulk-flow velocity evaluated at a point on the plasma boundary, meaning the last-closed flux surface or separatrix. It is not a flux-surface average and is signed in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal hydrogen velocity at the plasma boundary is the local component of the hydrogen species bulk-flow velocity tangent to the toroidal direction at a specified point on the last-closed flux surface or separatrix. The component is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is distinct from flux-surface-averaged boundary quantities such as [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) and [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), which average around the boundary rather than retaining the local value.

The local projection is

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{H}}(\mathbf{x}_b) = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{H}}(\mathbf{x}_b) \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{x}_b$ is the selected boundary position, specified by $R$ and $Z$ in meters and $\phi$ in radians; $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the hydrogen bulk velocity in m.s^-1; $\hat{\phi}$ is the dimensionless toroidal unit vector; and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{H}}$ is the toroidal component in m.s^-1.

In practice this quantity may be inferred from edge flow diagnostics, spectroscopic velocity measurements when applicable, or transport calculations constrained by edge plasma observations. Because it is local, it can vary with poloidal position along the separatrix and should not be substituted for a flux-surface average without an explicit averaging operation.

No universal numerical range applies at the separatrix because the value depends strongly on plasma current, toroidal field, collisionality, rotation sources, and edge momentum transport. Representative edge main-species toroidal speeds are often of order 10^3-10^4 m.s^-1, with values that may be near zero or may reverse sign locally.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the hydrogen bulk flow has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_iron_velocity_at_pedestal
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the iron impurity ion fluid velocity evaluated at the H-mode pedestal reference location. It represents the mean iron ion flow along the toroidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal iron velocity at the pedestal is the toroidal component of the mean fluid velocity of iron impurity ions at a reference position in the H-mode pedestal region. The pedestal is the narrow edge transport-barrier region where density, temperature, pressure, and rotation can vary rapidly across flux surfaces.

The component is defined by projecting the iron ion fluid velocity onto the toroidal basis direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}} = \mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{Fe}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the mean iron ion fluid velocity and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

In practice this quantity is commonly inferred from Doppler shifts of iron spectral lines, with corrections for viewing geometry, charge-state selection, and any modeled separation between toroidal and poloidal flow contributions. It may also be obtained from transport or equilibrium-constrained rotation analysis evaluated at the pedestal reference location.

Typical pedestal toroidal impurity velocities range from $-100$ to $100$ km.s$^{-1}$, equivalent to $-1 \times 10^5$ to $1 \times 10^5$ m.s$^{-1}$, depending on plasma current, torque input, collisional coupling, radial electric field, and edge transport conditions.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the iron ion fluid velocity component is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_iron_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the bulk flow velocity of iron impurity ions at the last closed flux surface, expressed in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Iron-ion toroidal velocity at the plasma boundary is the component of the bulk flow of iron impurity ions tangent to the toroidal direction at the last closed flux surface. It characterizes edge impurity momentum transport and rotation of a high-Z species, without implying a flux-surface average. The component is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The toroidal component is the projection of the iron ion fluid velocity onto the toroidal unit vector:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}} = \mathbf{u}_\mathrm{Fe} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_\mathrm{Fe}$ is the bulk iron ion velocity and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

In practice this quantity can be inferred from spectroscopic measurements of Doppler shifts of iron emission near the last closed flux surface, including charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy when suitable signals are available, or computed from edge impurity momentum-balance modeling. The value can vary with position on the boundary; no flux-surface averaging is part of this definition. Use toroidal_flux_surface_average_iron_velocity_at_plasma_boundary for the corresponding flux-surface-averaged boundary velocity, and [toroidal_iron_velocity_at_pedestal](name:toroidal_iron_velocity_at_pedestal) for the same species and component at the pedestal.

Typical magnitudes in tokamak edge plasmas are scenario dependent and often of order 10^3-10^4 m.s^-1; values near zero, sign reversals, and high-rotation cases reaching several 10^4 m.s^-1 can occur.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the iron ion bulk flow is directed toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_pedestal
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the krypton ion bulk flow velocity at the H-mode pedestal top, resolved along the direction of increasing phi in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame, where R is major radius, phi is toroidal angle, and Z is vertical height.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal krypton velocity at the pedestal is the signed toroidal component of the bulk-flow velocity of krypton ions evaluated at the H-mode pedestal top. The toroidal direction is the $\hat{\phi}$ basis direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is the krypton-specific pedestal quantity corresponding to the more general [toroidal ion velocity](name:toroidal_ion_velocity) and can be compared with [toroidal krypton velocity at the internal transport barrier](name:toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).

The scalar toroidal component is defined by projection of the krypton ion velocity vector onto the toroidal unit vector:

$$
v_\phi^{\mathrm{Kr}} = \mathbf{v}^{\mathrm{Kr}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $v_\phi^{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the signed toroidal scalar velocity in m.s$^{-1}$, $\mathbf{v}^{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the krypton ion bulk-flow velocity vector in m.s$^{-1}$, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle.

In practice this quantity is inferred from impurity-velocity measurements or calculations localized to the pedestal top. Spectroscopic determinations use Doppler shifts of krypton emission and viewing-geometry corrections to isolate the toroidal component; modeled values are obtained from impurity momentum balance or transport calculations constrained by edge plasma conditions.

No device-independent krypton-specific range is universal. Representative signed pedestal impurity toroidal velocities are often of order $10^3$-$10^5$ m.s$^{-1}$ in either toroidal direction, with values near zero indicating little resolved toroidal bulk flow.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the krypton ion bulk flow at the pedestal is along $+\hat{\phi}$, the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_pedestal
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short: Signed toroidal component of the lithium ion fluid velocity at the H-mode pedestal top in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame. It represents the local azimuthal rotation of lithium impurity ions at the steep-gradient edge transport barrier, not a pedestal average.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal lithium velocity at the pedestal is the local toroidal component of the lithium ion fluid velocity at the pedestal-top reference location, near the inner edge of the steep-gradient H-mode edge transport barrier. It is a signed component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; it is not a radial integral, volume average, or average over the full pedestal width.

The component is defined by projecting the lithium ion fluid velocity onto the toroidal unit vector:

$$
v_{\phi}^{\mathrm{Li}} = \mathbf{v}^{\mathrm{Li}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $v_{\phi}^{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the toroidal lithium velocity in m.s^-1, $\mathbf{v}^{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the lithium ion fluid velocity in m.s^-1, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the dimensionless unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

In practice, this quantity is commonly inferred from Doppler shifts of localized lithium line emission or charge-exchange emission, with corrections for viewing geometry, instrumental wavelength calibration, and the projection of the measured line-of-sight velocity onto $\hat{\phi}$. The pedestal-top reference location is determined from edge profile analysis, typically using the radial position at the top of the steep gradient region rather than a flux-surface average over the pedestal.

Representative pedestal impurity toroidal velocities are device- and scenario-dependent and may be near zero or of order $10^3-10^5$ m.s^-1 in tokamak H-mode plasmas. The value can change sign with the direction of toroidal rotation and may differ from main-ion rotation because lithium is an impurity species with its own charge state, source distribution, and collisional coupling.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the lithium ion fluid velocity component is in the $+\hat{\phi}$ direction, the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged toroidal component of the ionized lithium bulk flow velocity at the plasma boundary, the last closed flux surface. It is the projection onto the direction of increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame; neutral lithium is excluded and unresolved charge states are represented by a population-averaged ion flow.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal lithium velocity at the plasma boundary is the flux-surface-averaged toroidal projection of the ionized lithium bulk flow on the last closed flux surface. It characterizes edge impurity rotation and is governed by momentum balance, radial electric field effects, collisions with main ions, and external torque sources. The lithium population refers to ionized lithium; neutral lithium atoms are not included, and unresolved charge states are represented by a density-weighted ion-population flow.

The boundary value is defined by the flux-surface average of the toroidal projection over the last closed flux surface:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Li},b} = \frac{\displaystyle \oint_{\mathrm{LCFS}} \left(\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Li}} \cdot \hat{\phi}\right)\,\frac{dl}{B_p}}{\displaystyle \oint_{\mathrm{LCFS}} \frac{dl}{B_p}}
$$

where $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Li},b}$ is the boundary-averaged toroidal lithium ion velocity in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the bulk velocity of ionized lithium in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $dl$ is poloidal arc length on the last closed flux surface, and $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic-field magnitude. The $dl/B_p$ factor gives the flux-surface-average weighting for an axisymmetric boundary.

In practice this quantity can be inferred from spectroscopic Doppler measurements of lithium ion emission when suitable lines are available, or estimated by edge transport and momentum-balance modeling constrained by measurements. Local estimates are mapped to equilibrium flux surfaces, interpolated or extrapolated to the last closed flux surface or to the limiting closed-surface approach to it, and then averaged with the same $dl/B_p$ weighting. Analogous species-resolved boundary velocities include [toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), [toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), and [toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).

Typical boundary-averaged impurity toroidal velocities are strongly device- and regime-dependent. As an order-of-magnitude guide, edge values may be close to $0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, with absolute magnitudes of $10^3-10^4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ in rotating plasmas; substantially larger magnitudes are case-specific and usually indicate strong external torque or steep edge momentum gradients.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the lithium ion bulk flow has a toroidal component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_neon_velocity_at_pedestal
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the neon ion fluid velocity in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame, evaluated at the H-mode pedestal.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal neon velocity at the pedestal is the component of the neon ion fluid velocity along the toroidal direction, evaluated in the steep-gradient edge region characteristic of H-mode confinement. The pedestal lies near the outer edge of the confined plasma and is defined by strong radial gradients in quantities such as temperature, density, or pressure.

The toroidal component is the projection of the neon ion fluid velocity onto the toroidal basis direction:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Ne}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the neon ion fluid velocity in m.s^-1, $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}}$ is its toroidal component in m.s^-1, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

In practice, the pedestal location is identified from edge-gradient structure, and the neon toroidal flow is evaluated at that location from impurity-flow measurements or from impurity momentum-balance calculations. The value represents directed rotation of the neon impurity population rather than a thermal speed.

Typical absolute magnitudes for impurity toroidal flow at the pedestal are of order 10^3-10^5 m.s^-1 in tokamak edge plasmas, with the sign and magnitude depending on torque input, radial electric field, collisional coupling, and neoclassical transport.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the neon ion fluid velocity component points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the neon impurity-ion fluid velocity evaluated at the plasma boundary, projected along increasing toroidal angle phi in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame. It denotes a local boundary value, not an implicit flux-surface or separatrix average.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal neon velocity at the plasma boundary is the toroidal component of the neon impurity-ion fluid velocity evaluated on the last closed flux surface or separatrix. It describes azimuthal edge rotation of neon in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame and is a local boundary quantity; no flux-surface or separatrix average is implied.

The component is defined by projection of the neon ion fluid velocity onto the toroidal basis vector:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Ne}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the neon impurity-ion fluid velocity at the plasma boundary and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

This quantity may be inferred from Doppler spectroscopy or charge-exchange recombination measurements of neon line emission when suitable lines are available, or computed from impurity momentum-balance and edge-transport models. Because the name does not specify an ionization stage, it represents an elemental neon impurity-ion velocity; if a measurement is charge-state selective, interpreting it as the elemental neon velocity requires an explicit physical assumption about charge-state flow equilibration. A flux-surface average of this boundary velocity is a distinct quantity, represented by [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).

Typical edge impurity toroidal velocity magnitudes are of order $10^3$-$10^5$ m.s^-1 in tokamak plasmas, with values near zero possible in weakly rotating conditions. The magnitude and sign depend on momentum input, radial electric field shear, collisional coupling to main ions, and impurity transport near the separatrix.
NAMES.sign: Positive when neon ions flow in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_momentum_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Dimensionless factor applied to the toroidal component of neutral-particle momentum flux density in edge-plasma transport closures. It scales the component along increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame without defining the sign of that flux.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal neutral momentum coefficient is a dimensionless flux-limiter factor for the toroidal component of neutral-particle momentum transport. It is associated with momentum carried by neutral atoms or molecules along the $\phi$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The coefficient represents closure-model scaling of a signed toroidal momentum-flux density; it does not by itself define the direction or sign of that flux.

When used as a multiplicative limiter, its role can be written as:

$$
\Pi_{\phi,n}^{\mathrm{lim}} = C_{\phi,n}\,\Pi_{\phi,n}^{\mathrm{ref}}
$$

where $C_{\phi,n}$ is the dimensionless toroidal neutral momentum coefficient, $\Pi_{\phi,n}^{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reference or unmodified toroidal neutral momentum-flux density, and $\Pi_{\phi,n}^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the limited or effective toroidal neutral momentum-flux density. Both flux-density variables have units of $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, equivalently $\mathrm{N\,m^{-2}}$. The sign of the associated flux component is the sign of [toroidal_neutral_momentum_flux](name:toroidal_neutral_momentum_flux), while this coefficient only scales that component.

The coefficient is specified or computed within a neutral momentum-transport closure, for example from local collisionality, neutral mean free path, gradients, or a prescribed flux-limiting rule. It is not normally a directly measured observable; experimental information constrains it indirectly through comparisons between modeled and observed edge-plasma and neutral behavior.

Typical values are closure-specific dimensionless factors of order unity. In a purely attenuating limiter, $C_{\phi,n}=1$ leaves the reference toroidal momentum flux unchanged and $0 \le C_{\phi,n} \le 1$ reduces its magnitude; more general calibrated closures may define a different admissible interval, so the valid numerical range is part of the closure definition rather than a universal neutral-physics constant.

NAMES.name: toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_pedestal
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the nitrogen impurity ion fluid velocity evaluated at the H-mode pedestal reference location.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal velocity $v_{\phi,\mathrm{N}}$ of nitrogen impurity ions at the pedestal quantifies their rotation along the toroidal direction within the steep-gradient edge transport barrier characteristic of H-mode plasmas. Nitrogen is a low-Z impurity frequently injected into fusion devices for radiative power exhaust management, and its toroidal velocity at the pedestal reflects the combined influence of neoclassical impurity transport, momentum input from external heating, and ion-impurity friction.

The quantity is defined as the projection of the nitrogen ion fluid velocity vector onto the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{N}} = \mathbf{v}_\mathrm{N} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_\mathrm{N}$ is the nitrogen ion fluid velocity vector and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

This velocity component is commonly measured by charge exchange recombination spectroscopy (CXRS), in which the Doppler shift of nitrogen emission lines arising from charge-exchange reactions with an injected neutral beam gives the local ion flow velocity projected onto the toroidal direction. The pedestal value is a local evaluation at the reference flux surface of the H-mode pedestal, not a region average, consistent with the analogous quantities [toroidal_neon_velocity_at_pedestal](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_pedestal) and [toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_pedestal](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_pedestal). Radial profiles of nitrogen toroidal flow connect this pedestal value to [toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) and [toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the nitrogen ion flow is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ (counter-clockwise when viewed from above in the $+\hat{Z}$ direction).

NAMES.name: toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the nitrogen impurity ion velocity evaluated at the last closed flux surface (plasma boundary), characterizing edge impurity rotation at the separatrix.
NAMES.long:
Nitrogen ($\mathrm{N}$) is a seeding impurity used in tokamak edge plasmas for radiative cooling and divertor heat-load mitigation. The toroidal velocity of nitrogen ions at the plasma boundary (last closed flux surface) characterizes edge impurity rotation and enters momentum-balance models for the scrape-off layer boundary condition.

The quantity is defined as the projection of the nitrogen impurity ion fluid velocity onto the toroidal unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ at the separatrix:

$$
v_\phi^{\mathrm{N}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{N}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{N}}$ is the nitrogen impurity ion fluid velocity and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Measurement is typically performed by charge exchange recombination spectroscopy (CXRS), in which the Doppler shift of nitrogen emission lines yields the local toroidal velocity component; the separatrix position is determined by equilibrium reconstruction. The corresponding on-axis quantity is [toroidal nitrogen velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis); analogous boundary-velocity quantities for other seeding impurities include [toroidal_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) and [toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when $v_\phi^{\mathrm{N}}$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_pedestal
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the oxygen impurity ion fluid velocity at the H-mode pedestal reference location, projected along increasing toroidal angle phi in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal oxygen velocity at the pedestal is the toroidal component of the oxygen impurity ion fluid velocity evaluated at the edge pedestal reference location. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, it is the projection of the oxygen ion flow onto $\hat{\phi}$. It is used to compare impurity rotation with main-ion and other impurity rotation at the steep-gradient edge region.

For an oxygen ion charge state with charge number $Z_\mathrm{O}$, the toroidal velocity enters the radial force-balance relation:

$$
E_r = \frac{1}{Z_\mathrm{O} e n_\mathrm{O}} \frac{d p_\mathrm{O}}{d r} + v_{\phi,\mathrm{O}} B_\theta - v_{\theta,\mathrm{O}} B_\phi
$$

where $E_r$ is the radial electric field, $e$ is the elementary charge, $n_\mathrm{O}$ and $p_\mathrm{O}$ are the oxygen density and pressure, $r$ is a local outward radial coordinate across the pedestal, $v_{\phi,\mathrm{O}}$ is the toroidal oxygen velocity, $v_{\theta,\mathrm{O}}$ is the poloidal oxygen velocity, and $B_\theta$ and $B_\phi$ are the poloidal and toroidal magnetic-field components.

In experiments, this quantity is commonly inferred from Doppler shifts of oxygen charge-exchange recombination emission using viewing geometry that resolves the toroidal velocity component. It can also be obtained from edge equilibrium or transport analysis using measured impurity temperature, density, poloidal rotation, magnetic geometry, and radial electric field. Comparisons with [toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_pedestal](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_pedestal) and [toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_pedestal](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_pedestal) help distinguish main-ion rotation from impurity rotation and species-dependent neoclassical effects; comparisons with magnetic-axis and flux-surface-averaged oxygen velocities give radial rotation context.

Typical pedestal oxygen toroidal velocities are a few $10^3$ to $5 \times 10^4$ m.s^-1 in many tokamak plasmas, and can approach $10^5$ m.s^-1 in strongly torque-driven or high-intrinsic-rotation regimes. The magnitude and direction depend on momentum input, radial electric field, collisional coupling to main ions, and pedestal gradients.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the oxygen ion fluid velocity is directed along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the oxygen impurity ion bulk flow velocity evaluated at the plasma boundary (last closed flux surface).
NAMES.long:
The toroidal velocity of oxygen impurity ions at the plasma boundary quantifies the toroidal momentum carried by the oxygen ion population at the last closed flux surface, which separates the magnetically confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. This local point value is distinct from the flux-surface-averaged quantity [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_oxygen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_oxygen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), which integrates the velocity weighted by the boundary flux-surface geometry.

The toroidal component $v_\phi$ is the projection of the oxygen bulk flow velocity onto the toroidal direction:

$$
v_\phi = \mathbf{v}_\mathrm{O} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_\mathrm{O}$ is the oxygen ion bulk flow velocity and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Oxygen toroidal velocity at the boundary is primarily measured by charge exchange recombination spectroscopy (CXRS), exploiting the Doppler shift of oxygen emission lines to extract the ion flow velocity component along $\hat{\phi}$. Analogous boundary velocities for other impurity species include [toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) and [toroidal_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the oxygen ion flow is directed in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ (counter-clockwise when viewed from above in the $+\hat{Z}$ direction).

NAMES.name: toroidal_plasma_momentum_at_pedestal
NAMES.short: Total plasma momentum in the toroidal phi direction of the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame, summed over all ion species and electrons and evaluated at the pedestal top.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal plasma momentum at the pedestal top is the net linear momentum component along the toroidal direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is the pedestal-top value of the radial flux-surface function [toroidal_total_plasma_momentum](name:toroidal_total_plasma_momentum), summed over all ion species and electrons, and characterizes the rotation state at the edge transport barrier.

The scalar is the total toroidal plasma momentum function evaluated at the pedestal flux surface:

$$
P_\phi^{\mathrm{ped}} = P_\phi(\rho_{\mathrm{ped}}) = \int_{V(\rho_{\mathrm{ped}})} \sum_s m_s n_s(\mathbf{x}) v_{\phi,s}(\mathbf{x})\, dV
$$

where $P_\phi^{\mathrm{ped}}$ and $P_\phi$ have units kg m s^-1, $\rho_{\mathrm{ped}}$ is the pedestal-top value of a dimensionless radial flux-surface label such as the normalized toroidal flux radius $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$, $V(\rho_{\mathrm{ped}})$ is the plasma volume enclosed by that flux surface, $s$ indexes ion species and electrons, $m_s$ is species mass in kg, $n_s$ is number density in m^-3, $v_{\phi,s}$ is toroidal velocity in m s^-1, and $dV$ is the volume element in m^3.

In practice this quantity is derived from equilibrium geometry together with density, composition, and toroidal-flow estimates near the pedestal top. The pedestal-top flux surface is commonly identified from the edge pressure, temperature, or density gradient structure; ion flows may be constrained by spectroscopic measurements and momentum-balance modeling, while electron contributions are included in the species sum but are usually small because of the electron mass.

Typical absolute magnitudes are about 10^-2-10 kg m s^-1 in medium-size tokamaks, and can reach 10-100 kg m s^-1 in large, high-density plasmas or cases with strong external torque. Values close to zero occur for weak rotation or when counter-directed species contributions nearly cancel.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net toroidal plasma momentum points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_plasma_momentum_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Surface integral over the last closed magnetic flux surface of the major radius times the species-summed toroidal linear momentum density of all ion species and electrons. The boundary label specifies the surface over which the integration is performed; it is not a local point value, a flux-surface average, or an enclosed-volume integral.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal plasma momentum at the plasma boundary is the surface integral, taken over the last closed magnetic flux surface, of the major radius weighted species-summed toroidal linear momentum density of the plasma. It characterizes the net toroidal momentum content carried by the boundary flux surface, combining contributions from all ion species and electrons, and serves as an outer reference for momentum-transport and edge-rotation studies.

The boundary momentum is obtained by integrating the major-radius-weighted toroidal momentum density over the bounding surface:

$$
L_\phi^\mathrm{b} = \oint_{S_\mathrm{b}} R \sum_s m_s n_s v_{\phi,s} \, dS
$$

where $S_\mathrm{b}$ is the last closed magnetic flux surface, $R$ is the major radius in meters, $s$ runs over all ion species and electrons, $m_s$ is the species mass in kilograms, $n_s$ is the species number density in m^-3, and $v_{\phi,s} = \mathbf{v}_s \cdot \hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal velocity component in m.s^-1 in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with $R$ major radius, $\phi$ toroidal angle, and $Z$ vertical height. The integrand $R \sum_s m_s n_s v_{\phi,s}$ has units of kg.m^-1.s^-1, so its surface integral has units of kg.m.s^-1. Equivalently, this quantity equals the boundary surface area multiplied by the flux-surface average of the major-radius-weighted toroidal momentum density.

In practice this quantity is reconstructed by combining species density and toroidal-rotation information with the reconstructed plasma geometry of the boundary flux surface, then applying the major-radius weighting and surface integration. Ion toroidal velocities are commonly constrained by spectroscopic rotation measurements, while species contributions that are not directly measured are inferred from transport, quasineutrality, and momentum-balance modeling.

Typical absolute magnitudes range from roughly $10^{-3}$-$1$ kg.m.s^-1 in small and medium-size tokamaks and may reach larger values in strongly rotating or large-volume plasmas; values near zero occur when co-current and counter-current contributions nearly cancel.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net toroidal momentum points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_total_momentum_flux
NAMES.short: Toroidal component, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame, of the total edge-plasma momentum-flux density. It is a stress-like flux per unit area for toroidal momentum transport, including advective, pressure, viscous, and modeled turbulent stress contributions; it is not a momentum inventory or torque source.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal total momentum flux is the flux-density component associated with transport of toroidal momentum in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It has the dimensions of stress or pressure: momentum transported per unit time per unit area. "Total" means that all included particle species and modeled transport mechanisms are combined; it does not denote a volume-integrated momentum content or a momentum source.

A useful continuum definition is the $\phi$-projected component of the total momentum-flux tensor across a surface whose positive normal is $+\hat{\phi}$:

$$
F_{\phi}^{\mathrm{tot}} = \hat{\phi}\cdot \left[\sum_s\left(\rho_s\mathbf{u}_s\mathbf{u}_s + p_s\mathbf{I} + \boldsymbol{\pi}_s + \boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{turb}}_s\right)\right]\cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $s$ labels species, $\rho_s$ is mass density in kg.m^-3, $\mathbf{u}_s$ is fluid velocity in m.s^-1, $\mathbf{u}_s\mathbf{u}_s$ is a dyadic product, $p_s$ is scalar pressure in kg.m^-1.s^-2, $\mathbf{I}$ is the identity tensor, and $\boldsymbol{\pi}_s$ and $\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{turb}}_s$ are viscous and modeled turbulent stress tensors in kg.m^-1.s^-2. The first $\hat{\phi}$ selects the transported toroidal momentum component and the second specifies the positive toroidal flux direction. A radial flux of toroidal momentum would instead use the $\hat{R}$ surface-normal projection, and is conceptually distinct from convective quantities such as [toroidal_momentum_convection_velocity](name:toroidal_momentum_convection_velocity).

In practice this quantity is computed from edge-plasma momentum balance models by summing species moments, pressure terms, collisional stresses, and closure-dependent turbulent stresses. It may be constrained indirectly by measurements of density, temperature, impurity content, neutral populations, and flow velocities, but it is rarely measured as a single direct diagnostic observable. It should not be confused with [toroidal_neutral_momentum](name:toroidal_neutral_momentum), which describes toroidal momentum carried by neutrals, or with torque/source terms such as [toroidal_neutral_torque_density](name:toroidal_neutral_torque_density).

Order-of-magnitude values follow pressure and dynamic-pressure scales. In scrape-off-layer and divertor conditions, absolute magnitudes commonly span about $10^{-3}$-$10^{2}$ kg.m^-1.s^-2, while pedestal or high-density edge regions can reach $10^{2}$-$10^{4}$ kg.m^-1.s^-2. The exact value is strongly dependent on species composition, flow speed, temperature, collisionality, and the turbulent-stress closure used.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $+\hat{\phi}$ toroidal momentum is transported across a surface of constant $\phi$ along the $+\hat{\phi}$ normal, toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_total_plasma_momentum_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Surface integral of the toroidal component of plasma linear momentum at the last closed flux surface in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame, summed over all ion species and electrons. It is a signed total linear momentum, not toroidal angular momentum.
NAMES.long:
The total toroidal plasma momentum at the plasma boundary is the toroidal component of plasma linear momentum assigned to the separatrix or last closed flux surface, summed over all ion species and electrons. The toroidal component is taken along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. This is not toroidal angular momentum; no factor of $R$ multiplies the toroidal velocity.

For a surface-integrated boundary value, the defining linear-momentum form is

$$
P_{\phi,b} = \int_{S_b} \sum_s \Sigma_s(\mathbf{x})\,u_{\phi,s}(\mathbf{x})\,dA
$$

where $S_b$ is the boundary flux surface, $dA$ is the area element on $S_b$ in m^2, $s$ labels plasma species, $\Sigma_s$ is the species mass per unit boundary-surface area in kg m^-2, and $u_{\phi,s}$ is the toroidal component of species flow velocity in m s^-1. If the value is derived from volume fields, $\Sigma_s$ represents the mass density $m_s n_s$ integrated through the boundary shell normal to $S_b$, with $m_s$ in kg and $n_s$ in m^-3.

In analysis, this quantity is computed from edge species densities, composition, toroidal flow velocities, and the geometry of the boundary flux surface. It is the boundary counterpart of the radial quantity [toroidal_total_plasma_momentum](name:toroidal_total_plasma_momentum), while toroidal_flux_surface_average_total_plasma_momentum_at_plasma_boundary gives the corresponding flux-surface average rather than the surface-integrated total. Rotation measurements such as charge-exchange or Doppler spectroscopy are typically combined with density and impurity-content estimates to infer the ion contribution; the electron contribution is usually much smaller because of the electron mass.

Typical absolute values for separatrix-associated boundary integrals are often about 10^-6-10^-2 kg.m.s^-1 in medium-size tokamak edge analyzes, but the value can be near zero for balanced rotation and can be larger in strongly torque-driven or larger plasmas. The magnitude scales with edge density, ion mass, toroidal flow speed, boundary surface area, and the thickness or surface measure used to assign mass to the boundary surface.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net toroidal plasma linear momentum points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the tritium ion fluid velocity evaluated at the plasma boundary, the last closed flux surface separating the magnetically confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal tritium velocity at the plasma boundary gives the bulk rotational flow of tritium ions projected onto the toroidal direction $\hat{\phi}$, evaluated at the last closed flux surface where the confined plasma meets the scrape-off layer. This boundary value constrains the outer edge of the radial tritium rotation profile and reflects the balance between momentum injection, viscous transport across the pedestal, and ion-neutral friction at the plasma edge.

The defining relation is the projection of the tritium ion fluid velocity vector $\mathbf{v}_T$ onto $\hat{\phi}$ at the last closed flux surface:

$$
v_{\phi,T}^{\rm b} = \mathbf{v}_T \cdot \hat{\phi}\Big|_{\rm LCFS}
$$

where $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with $R$ the major radius and $Z$ the vertical height.

The toroidal ion velocity at the boundary is measured by charge exchange recombination spectroscopy (CXRS), inferring the flow from Doppler shifts of charge-exchange emission lines in the steep-gradient edge region. For tritium-containing plasmas, measurements carry additional constraints due to the radioactive nature of the fuel species. Edge toroidal ion velocities in tokamak plasmas range from ~1 km/s in L-mode to ~100 km/s in strongly heated H-mode discharges. Comparing this quantity with [toroidal tritium velocity at the pedestal](name:toroidal_tritium_velocity_at_pedestal) and [toroidal tritium velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_tritium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) characterizes the full radial rotation profile; [toroidal helium-3 velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) provides the analogous boundary quantity for the helium-3 species.
NAMES.sign: Positive when tritium ions flow in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ (counter-clockwise when viewed from the $+\hat{Z}$ direction).

NAMES.name: toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_pedestal
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the flow velocity of tungsten impurity ions evaluated at the H-mode pedestal top.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal velocity of tungsten impurity ions at the pedestal top characterizes the $\hat{\phi}$-direction rotation of this high-Z impurity species at the steep-gradient edge transport barrier. Tungsten enters the confined plasma primarily through erosion of plasma-facing components in metal-wall devices, and its toroidal rotation at the pedestal reflects neoclassical impurity transport, ion–impurity friction, and externally applied toroidal momentum.

The radial force balance for the tungsten ion population links the toroidal velocity to the local radial electric field $E_r$:

$$
E_r = \frac{1}{Z_W e n_W} \frac{\partial p_W}{\partial r} + v_{\phi,W} B_\theta - v_{\theta,W} B_\phi
$$

where $Z_W$ is the mean tungsten charge state, $e$ is the elementary charge, $n_W$ is the tungsten number density (see [tungsten density at the pedestal](name:tungsten_density_at_pedestal)), $p_W$ is the tungsten pressure, $B_\theta$ and $B_\phi$ are the poloidal and toroidal magnetic field components, and $v_{\theta,W}$ is the poloidal tungsten velocity.

This quantity is measured by charge exchange recombination spectroscopy (CXRS) from Doppler shifts of tungsten emission lines localized to the pedestal region. Toroidal impurity rotation at the pedestal in H-mode plasmas reaches magnitudes of order $10^3$–$10^4$ m/s, with sign and magnitude determined by the momentum input scenario. The same species velocity at other radial locations is given by [toroidal tungsten velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) and [at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_plasma_boundary); the analogous quantity for xenon is [toroidal xenon velocity at the pedestal](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_pedestal).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the tungsten ion flow is directed in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the tungsten impurity ion fluid velocity in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame, evaluated at the last closed flux surface separating confined plasma from the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal tungsten velocity at the plasma boundary is the component of the tungsten impurity ion fluid velocity along the toroidal direction at the last closed flux surface, the surface separating confined plasma from the scrape-off layer. The component is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The defining projection is:

$$
v_{\phi,W}^{\mathrm{LCFS}} = \left.\mathbf{v}_W \cdot \hat{\phi}\right|_{\mathrm{LCFS}}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_W$ is the tungsten ion fluid velocity, $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle, and LCFS denotes the last closed flux surface.

Experimentally, this velocity is commonly inferred from Doppler shifts of tungsten spectral lines using edge spectroscopy or charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy when suitable tungsten emission is available. In modeling and equilibrium-coupled transport analysis, it is obtained by projecting the impurity fluid velocity onto $\hat{\phi}$ or by solving an impurity momentum balance including electric-field forces, pressure-gradient effects, collisional friction with the main ions, and momentum sources.

Typical tokamak edge values are about $10^3-5 \times 10^4$ m.s^-1, with the sign and magnitude depending on bulk plasma rotation, radial electric field, collisionality, charge-state distribution, and pedestal conditions. This pointwise boundary quantity is distinguished from the flux-surface average [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_tungsten_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_tungsten_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), and it uses the same toroidal-component convention as related species velocities such as [toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), [toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), and [toroidal_electron_velocity](name:toroidal_electron_velocity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the tungsten ion fluid velocity points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_pedestal
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the xenon ion bulk flow velocity at the H-mode pedestal-top reference location, resolved along increasing toroidal angle phi in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal xenon velocity at the pedestal is the toroidal component of the xenon ion bulk fluid velocity in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when viewed from the $+\hat{Z}$ side, and $Z$ is vertical height. The evaluation location is the H-mode pedestal-top reference flux surface, the core-side edge of the steep-gradient pedestal region inside the separatrix. The radial label for this reference location is typically a dimensionless normalized toroidal flux radius $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ or normalized poloidal flux $\psi_N$, distinguishing it from the pedestal foot and the separatrix.

The projection defining the toroidal component is

$$
v_\phi^{\mathrm{Xe}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Xe}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the xenon ion bulk velocity vector in m.s^-1, $v_\phi^{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the resulting scalar component in m.s^-1, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the dimensionless unit vector along increasing $\phi$.

In practice, this quantity is obtained on the pedestal-top flux surface from spectroscopic velocity measurements when identifiable xenon lines and suitable viewing geometry are available, or from impurity momentum-balance calculations constrained by measured profiles. Charge-exchange or passive Doppler spectroscopy measures line-of-sight velocities; geometric projection and mapping to the pedestal-top flux-surface label separate the toroidal component.

The same toroidal projection applies at other radial reference locations, such as [toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) and [toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary). Pedestal comparisons with [toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_pedestal](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_pedestal), [toroidal_neon_velocity_at_pedestal](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_pedestal), and [toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_pedestal](name:toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_pedestal) help distinguish species-dependent impurity rotation from common edge momentum flow.

Typical pedestal impurity toroidal velocities are strongly scenario-dependent. Values near 0 m.s^-1 can occur in weakly rotating or braked plasmas, while rotating H-mode edge plasmas often have magnitudes of order 10^3-10^4 m.s^-1; stronger external momentum input can produce larger magnitudes. These values are order-of-magnitude context rather than a xenon-specific limit.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the xenon ion bulk flow component points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the xenon ion bulk flow velocity at the plasma boundary, the last closed flux surface separating the confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal xenon velocity at the plasma boundary is the $\hat{\phi}$-component of the xenon impurity ion fluid velocity, evaluated as a flux-surface average on the last closed flux surface (separatrix). It quantifies the net toroidal rotation of the xenon ion population at the transition between the closed-field-line confined region and the open-field-line scrape-off layer.

The toroidal velocity component is defined as:

$$
v_\phi^{\rm Xe} = \mathbf{v}_{\rm Xe} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\rm Xe}$ is the xenon ion fluid velocity and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Xenon impurity ion velocities at the plasma boundary are typically inferred from the Doppler shift of charge exchange recombination spectroscopy lines, or from passive spectroscopy of xenon ion emission at the plasma edge. Xenon is a heavy noble-gas impurity with atomic number $Z = 54$, used for radiative plasma cooling and seeding; its large mass and high charge states make the toroidal velocity measurement sensitive to local momentum balance and neoclassical transport at the separatrix. Analogous boundary toroidal velocities for other impurity species include [toroidal krypton velocity](name:toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), [toroidal neon velocity](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), and [toroidal carbon velocity](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when xenon ions flow in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ (counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$).

NAMES.name: total_ion_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Radial e-folding length of the total ion number density in the scrape-off layer, defined as the inverse magnitude of its logarithmic gradient evaluated perpendicular to flux surfaces. The total ion density is the sum over all ion species and charge states, so this scale length is intrinsically non-negative.
NAMES.long:
Total ion decay length over the scrape-off layer is the characteristic distance over which the total ion number density falls by a factor of $e$ moving outward across the open-field-line region beyond the last closed flux surface. The total ion number density is the sum of densities over all ion species and charge states, so this quantity describes how rapidly the combined ion population connected to open magnetic field lines decays toward the wall.

The decay length is defined as the inverse magnitude of the logarithmic gradient of the total ion density along the local outward distance perpendicular to flux surfaces:

$$
\lambda_{n_i,\mathrm{tot}} = \left| \frac{d}{d r_\perp} \ln n_{i,\mathrm{tot}} \right|^{-1}
$$

where $r_\perp$ is the local distance measured perpendicular to the flux surfaces, increasing outward from the last closed flux surface toward the wall (in meters), and $n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total ion number density (in $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$). The total ion density is $n_{i,\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_a \sum_Z n_{a,Z}$, where $n_{a,Z}$ is the density of ion species $a$ in charge state $Z$. Taking the magnitude makes the scale length non-negative regardless of the chosen sign of the radial coordinate.

In practice this quantity is obtained by reconstructing the total ion density across the scrape-off layer from charge-resolved ion measurements, edge plasma modeling, or quasineutrality and composition assumptions, then evaluating the local logarithmic gradient or fitting an exponential fall-off over a specified radial interval. A fitted value represents an effective decay length over that interval rather than a strictly local derivative.

Representative scrape-off-layer ion density decay lengths in tokamak edge analyzes are commonly of order $0.001\text{--}0.05\ \mathrm{m}$, with the value depending on plasma current, connection length, collisionality, recycling, detachment state, and the radial interval used for evaluation.

NAMES.name: total_ion_density_at_pedestal
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Total ion number density summed over all ion species and charge states, evaluated at the H-mode pedestal top.
NAMES.long:
The total ion density at the pedestal is the combined number density of all ion species and charge states in the H-mode edge transport barrier, the steep-gradient region where pressure, temperature, and density rise sharply inward from the scrape-off layer toward the confined core.

The quantity is defined as:

$$
n_{i,\text{tot}} = \sum_{s} n_s
$$

where $n_s$ is the number density of ion species $s$, summed over all its charge states, in m$^{-3}$. In a pure deuterium plasma this reduces to the electron density; in impurity-seeded discharges, $n_{i,\text{tot}}$ differs from $n_e$ according to the quasineutrality relation $n_e = \sum_s Z_s n_s$, where $Z_s$ is the charge number of species $s$.

The pedestal ion density is inferred from charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy, Thomson scattering, or reflectometry, frequently combined with the quasineutrality constraint to partition contributions among individual species. It is a key parameter governing pedestal stability and ELM onset.

Typical values in H-mode discharges range from $1 \times 10^{19}$ to $2 \times 10^{20}$ m$^{-3}$, depending on machine size, fueling rate, and impurity content. Species-resolved contributions are captured by [deuterium_density_at_pedestal](name:deuterium_density_at_pedestal) and [carbon_density_at_pedestal](name:carbon_density_at_pedestal), while the radial context is provided by [total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary) and [total_ion_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:total_ion_density_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the total ion number density corresponds to a physically present, net positive ion population per unit volume.

NAMES.name: total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Unweighted sum of number densities of all charged ion species evaluated locally at the plasma boundary or last closed flux surface. Neutral particles are excluded, and each ion population contributes by particle density rather than by charge.
NAMES.long:
Total ion density at the plasma boundary is the local particle density obtained by summing the number densities of all charged ion species at the last closed flux surface. The sum is unweighted: each ion contributes one particle to the total regardless of charge state, while neutral atoms and molecules are excluded. This is a local boundary quantity, not a flux-surface average unless averaging is stated explicitly.

The total ion density at the plasma boundary is defined by the species sum

$$
n_{i,\mathrm{tot},b} = \sum_s n_{i,s,b}
$$

where $n_{i,\mathrm{tot},b}$ is the total ion density at the boundary in $\mathrm{m}^{-3}$, $n_{i,s,b}$ is the number density of charged ion species $s$ at the boundary in $\mathrm{m}^{-3}$, and the sum runs over all charged ion species or charge-state-resolved ion populations included in the plasma composition.

In practice this quantity is obtained from edge diagnostic interpretation or from boundary values in transport and equilibrium-coupled edge modeling. Electron density and quasi-neutrality can constrain the charge-weighted ion sum, but they do not by themselves define this unweighted total unless the ion composition and charge states are also known.

Typical values at the last closed flux surface in tokamak plasmas are about $1 \times 10^{18}-1 \times 10^{20}\ \mathrm{m}^{-3}$, depending on fueling, confinement regime, plasma current, and edge transport conditions.

NAMES.name: tritium_density_at_pedestal
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short: Tritium ion number density evaluated at the H-mode pedestal top.
NAMES.long:
Tritium density at the pedestal is the local number density of ionized tritium at the H-mode pedestal top. The pedestal top is the radial location where the steep-gradient edge transport barrier transitions to the flatter core density distribution, so this value characterizes the tritium content just inside the barrier.

The local number-density definition evaluated at that location is:

$$
n_{T,\mathrm{ped}} = \left.\frac{dN_T}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{ped}}
$$

where $dN_T$ is the number of tritium ions in the infinitesimal volume $dV$, $dV$ is measured in $\mathrm{m}^3$, and the subscript $\mathrm{ped}$ means that the limit is taken at the pedestal-top location.

In practice, this value is obtained by identifying the pedestal top from the edge density or pressure structure and evaluating the tritium ion density there. If the tritium component is not resolved independently, it may be inferred from the total ion density together with the local isotopic fraction, so $n_{T,\mathrm{ped}}$ reflects both the pedestal density and the fuel mix.

Typical values are zero in plasmas without tritium fueling or with negligible tritium inventory.
