Perpendicular momentum flux due to perturbed parallel magnetic field is the dimensionless contribution to turbulent toroidal gyrocenter momentum transport carried by the $\delta B_\parallel$ compressional electromagnetic perturbation through gyrocenter motion perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field. The transported momentum is the toroidal gyrocenter momentum associated with the angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and the radial flux is the projection along increasing $\rho$ in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$.

A compact normalized form is:

$$
\hat{\Pi}_{\phi,\perp}^{\delta B_\parallel}
=
\frac{\Pi_{\phi,\perp}^{\delta B_\parallel}}{\Pi_\mathrm{ref}}
=
\sum_{\mathbf{k}_\perp}\sum_s
\left\langle
\int d\hat{\Lambda}_s\,
\hat{p}_{\phi,s}\,
\operatorname{Re}\!\left[
\hat{g}_{s,\mathbf{k}_\perp}^{*}
\hat{v}_{\rho,\perp,s,\mathbf{k}_\perp}^{\delta B_\parallel}
\right]
\right\rangle_{\rho,t}
$$

where $\Pi_{\phi,\perp}^{\delta B_\parallel}$ is the physical perpendicular toroidal momentum flux from the $\delta B_\parallel$ channel, $\Pi_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference momentum-flux scale, $s$ labels species, $d\hat{\Lambda}_s$ is the normalized velocity-space measure including the gyrocenter Jacobian, $\hat{p}_{\phi,s}$ is normalized toroidal gyrocenter momentum, $\hat{g}_{s,\mathbf{k}_\perp}$ is the normalized non-adiabatic gyrocenter distribution perturbation, and $\hat{v}_{\rho,\perp,s,\mathbf{k}_\perp}^{\delta B_\parallel}$ is the normalized radial projection of the perpendicular gyrocenter velocity driven by $\delta B_\parallel$. The hats indicate quantities scaled so that the phase-space integral has the same normalization as $\Pi_{\phi,\perp}^{\delta B_\parallel}/\Pi_\mathrm{ref}$, and the sum is over the retained perpendicular wavevectors.

This quantity is computed by isolating the $\delta B_\parallel$ terms in the electromagnetic gyrocenter equations, forming the toroidal-momentum moment of the non-adiabatic gyrocenter distribution, averaging over the turbulent state or eigenmode phase, and summing the spectral contributions. It is the perpendicular-channel counterpart of [parallel_momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field](name:parallel_momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field), contributes to the $\delta B_\parallel$ momentum-flux decomposition represented by [momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field](name:momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field), and is distinct from the perturbed-parallel-vector-potential channel [perpendicular_momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential](name:perpendicular_momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential). In rotating-frame formulations, $\hat{p}_{\phi,s}$ and the corresponding radial drift are evaluated relative to that rotating frame.

Typical normalized absolute values in core gyrokinetic turbulence are often of order $10^{-4}$-$10^{-1}$, with the largest contributions occurring when electromagnetic compressional fluctuations are appreciable. The sign and magnitude are sensitive to plasma beta, magnetic geometry, rotation-gradient drive, and the cross phase between $\delta B_\parallel$ and the gyrocenter distribution response.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the $\delta B_\parallel$-driven perpendicular flux transports positive toroidal gyrocenter momentum outward, toward increasing $\rho$ in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, where positive toroidal momentum is in the direction of increasing $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_energy
NAMES.short: Dimensionless velocity-space moment of the perturbed particle distribution weighted by 0.5 times the species mass, the squared perpendicular speed, and the total speed squared. It measures the perpendicular-speed-weighted kinetic response of a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode relative to the chosen normalization.
NAMES.long:
Perpendicular normalized particle perturbed energy is a dimensionless moment of the perturbed particle distribution for a species in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode. Its weighting is the total kinetic-energy factor multiplied by squared speed perpendicular to the local magnetic field; it is not the product of perpendicular kinetic energy and total kinetic energy.

The normalized moment may be written as

$$
M_{\perp E,s} = \frac{1}{N_{\perp E,s}} \int \frac{1}{2} m_s v_\perp^2 v^2 \, \delta f_s(\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the species mass, $v_\perp$ is the particle speed perpendicular to the local magnetic field, $v^2 = v_\parallel^2 + v_\perp^2$ is the total speed squared, $\delta f_s$ is the perturbed particle distribution with units $s^3 m^{-6}$, and $d^3v$ has units $m^3 s^{-3}$. The normalization factor $N_{\perp E,s}$ has units $kg\,m\,s^{-4}$, matching the unnormalized integral, so that $M_{\perp E,s}$ has unit 1.

This quantity is computed from the velocity-space representation of the linear eigenfunction by numerical quadrature over $\delta f_s$. It is mainly used to compare how strongly different species or modes populate high-perpendicular-speed parts of velocity space, relative to the selected eigenmode normalization.

No device-independent numerical range is physically meaningful for this normalized moment. A linear eigenmode can be multiplied by an arbitrary real or complex amplitude, and this moment scales by the same factor; therefore only comparisons made with the same normalization and eigenfunction phase convention are physically meaningful.

NAMES.name: perturbed_gyrocenter_pressure
NAMES.subject: gyrocenter
NAMES.short: Second velocity-space moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution function, characterizing the departure of the gyrotropic pressure tensor from its equilibrium value in gyrokinetic turbulence. This parent generalizes over parallel and perpendicular components and over dimensional or normalized representations.
NAMES.long:
The perturbed gyrocenter pressure is the perturbed component of the gyrotropic pressure tensor, obtained as the second-order velocity-space moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution function δf. It represents the local deviation of the gyrocenter pressure from the equilibrium pressure profile due to electrostatic and electromagnetic fluctuations.

The dimensional form of the pressure moment for a species s is defined by the integral over velocity space:

$$
\delta p_s = \int m_s \, v^2 \, \delta f_s \, d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the species mass, $v$ is the velocity magnitude, and $\delta f_s$ is the perturbed distribution. The moment may be taken along the parallel direction ($v_\parallel$) or perpendicular direction ($v_\perp$), corresponding to $\delta p_{\parallel,s}$ and $\delta p_{\perp,s}$ respectively. Specific standard names provide normalized versions where the moment is divided by a reference thermal pressure $n_\mathrm{ref} T_\mathrm{ref}$, yielding a dimensionless quantity.

This moment is computed in gyrokinetic simulations and eigenmode solvers as a diagnostic of the pressure response to turbulence. It complements the perturbed gyrocenter density in the low-order moment hierarchy.

Typical values in the core of a medium-size tokamak range from 0.1–10% of the equilibrium pressure for quasilinear turbulence levels, corresponding to $\delta p / p_\mathrm{eq} \sim 10^{-3}$–$10^{-1}$ for dimensional forms, or equivalent dimensionless values of $10^{-4}$–$10^{-2}$ relative to the reference pressure.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the perturbed gyrocenter pressure represents a local enhancement above the equilibrium pressure profile.

NAMES.name: normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure
NAMES.subject: gyrocenter
NAMES.short: Two-component vector of the normalized pressure moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution, with components parallel and perpendicular to the local magnetic field, each normalized to a reference thermal pressure.
NAMES.long:
The normalized gyrocenter perturbed pressure is a vector quantity collecting the dimensionless parallel and perpendicular thermal-pressure responses of the non-equilibrium part of the gyrocenter distribution function $\delta f_s$ for a single plasma species, normalized to a reference thermal pressure $p_{\mathrm{ref}} = n_{\mathrm{ref}} T_{\mathrm{ref}}$. It generalizes the scalar gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure to the full anisotropic pressure decomposition along and across the local magnetic field direction $\hat{b}$.

The two components are defined as velocity-space integrals:

$$
\hat{p}_{\parallel/\perp,\,s} = \frac{m_s}{p_{\mathrm{ref}}} \int w_{\parallel/\perp}\, \delta f_s\, d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the species mass, the weight $w_\parallel = v_\parallel^2$ defines the parallel component (see [parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure](name:parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure)) and $w_\perp = v_\perp^2/2$ defines the perpendicular gyrotropic component (see [perpendicular_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure](name:perpendicular_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure)), with $v_\parallel$ and $v_\perp$ the velocity projections along and across $\hat{b}$ respectively.

This vector is computed in gyrokinetic simulations as part of the velocity-space moment hierarchy characterizing pressure anisotropy driven by electromagnetic fluctuations. Gyroaveraged variants incorporating finite-Larmor-radius corrections are provided by perpendicular_normalized_gyrocenter_gyroaveraged_pressure and parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_gyroaveraged_pressure.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the perturbed gyrocenter distribution function increases the respective pressure moment above the equilibrium reference value.

NAMES.name: parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure
NAMES.subject: gyrocenter
NAMES.short: Normalized parallel pressure moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution for a species, formed by weighting the perturbation with the square of velocity along the local magnetic field. It measures the dimensionless parallel thermal-pressure response of a gyrokinetic eigenmode.
NAMES.long:
Parallel normalized gyrocenter perturbed pressure is the parallel component of the gyrotropic pressure perturbation obtained from the perturbed gyrocenter distribution. It measures the change in thermal pressure associated with gyrocenter motion along the local magnetic field, normalized to a reference scalar pressure.

The defining moment is the full velocity-space integral of the parallel kinetic-energy weighting of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution:

$$
\tilde{p}_{\parallel,g} = \frac{1}{p_\mathrm{ref}} \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} m v_\parallel^2 \, \delta\bar{f}(\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $m$ is the species mass, $v_\parallel$ is the gyrocenter velocity component along the local magnetic field, $\delta\bar{f}$ is the perturbed gyrocenter distribution, and $p_\mathrm{ref}=n_\mathrm{ref}T_\mathrm{ref}$ with $T_\mathrm{ref}$ expressed as an energy. The integral is over all three velocity components, not only over $v_\parallel$; $\delta\bar{f}$ has units of density per velocity-space volume, so $\int \delta\bar{f}\,d^3v$ has units of number density.

In delta-f gyrokinetic calculations this moment is evaluated for each species and fluctuation or eigenmode to characterize the parallel thermal-energy part of the response. As a gyrocenter moment it is defined after gyroaveraging; the related particle-frame pressure moment also includes the transformation from gyrocenter to particle position. Together with [perpendicular_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure](name:perpendicular_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure), it specifies the gyrotropic pressure perturbation in the gyrocenter frame.

Typical absolute fluctuation levels in saturated core microturbulence are often $10^{-4}-10^{-2}$ when normalized to the equilibrium pressure, while edge or strongly driven cases can be larger. In linear eigenmode studies the absolute amplitude is set by the chosen eigenfunction normalization, so order-unity values may reflect normalization rather than a physical fluctuation level.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the perturbed gyrocenter distribution increases the $m v_\parallel^2$ velocity-space moment above its equilibrium value.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure
NAMES.subject: gyrocenter
NAMES.short: Dimensionless perpendicular gyrotropic pressure moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution function for a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, normalized to a reference thermal pressure.
NAMES.long:
The perpendicular normalized gyrocenter perturbed pressure is the second velocity-space moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution function $\delta f_s$, integrated with the perpendicular kinetic-energy weight and normalized by a reference thermal pressure $p_{\mathrm{ref}} = n_{\mathrm{ref}} T_{\mathrm{ref}}$. It characterizes the perturbation to the gyrotropic pressure component in the plane orthogonal to the background magnetic field $\mathbf{B}_0$ for a given linear gyrokinetic eigenmode.

The defining velocity-space integral is:

$$
\delta \tilde{p}_{\perp} = \frac{1}{p_{\mathrm{ref}}} \int \frac{m_s v_{\perp}^2}{2} \, \delta f_s \, d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the particle mass, $v_{\perp}$ is the gyrocenter speed perpendicular to $\mathbf{B}_0$, and $\delta f_s$ is the perturbed gyrocenter distribution function. The absence of the $J_0(k_{\perp} \rho_s)$ gyroaveraging factor distinguishes this moment from normalized_perpendicular_gyroaveraged_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure, where $k_{\perp}$ is the perpendicular wavenumber and $\rho_s$ is the species Larmor radius.

This moment is computed in local delta-f flux-tube gyrokinetic simulations as part of the linear eigenmode structure. It is the second (perpendicular) entry of the ordered component pair in [normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure](name:normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure), complementing [parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure](name:parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure) which carries the parallel component. Together these two moments fully characterize the gyrotropic pressure response of each kinetic species to the eigenmode perturbation.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the perturbed gyrocenter distribution contributes a net increase in perpendicular thermal pressure relative to the local equilibrium value.

NAMES.name: perturbed_pressure
NAMES.short: Isotropic trace-averaged pressure perturbation of a plasma kinetic distribution function, serving as the parent concept for species- and representation-specific perturbed pressure moments in gyrokinetic turbulence.
NAMES.long:
The perturbed pressure is the scalar isotropic second moment of the deviation $\delta f_s$ of a kinetic distribution function from its local equilibrium, collapsing the parallel and perpendicular pressure fluctuations into a single scalar measure. It generalizes over the particle-frame and gyrocenter-frame representations, and may be expressed dimensionally or normalized to a local equilibrium reference.

The principal defining relation for species $s$ is:

$$
\delta p_s = \frac{1}{3} \int m_s \left|\mathbf{v} - \mathbf{u}_s\right|^2 \delta f_s(\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the species mass, $\mathbf{u}_s$ is the mean fluid velocity, and $\delta f_s$ is the non-equilibrium component of the distribution function. When divided by the local equilibrium pressure $p_{s,0}$, the result is the dimensionless form with unit 1.

In gyrokinetic turbulence calculations, this moment is computed either from the perturbed particle distribution or from the guiding-center (gyrocenter) distribution. The particle_perturbed_pressure combines the parallel and two perpendicular velocity-moment contributions of the perturbed particle distribution into one scalar, while the gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure is the corresponding gyrocenter-frame moment that incorporates finite-Larmor-radius corrections via gyroaveraging. The explicitly normalized form is documented in normalized_perturbed_pressure.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $\delta f_s$ increases the local pressure above the equilibrium value $p_{s,0}$.

NAMES.name: normalized_perturbed_pressure
NAMES.short: Dimensionless total isotropic pressure moment of the perturbed particle distribution function for a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, normalized by the equilibrium species reference pressure.
NAMES.long:
The normalized perturbed pressure is the dimensionless isotropic trace of the pressure tensor perturbation carried by the particle distribution function for a single plasma species in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode. It captures the second velocity-space moment of the non-equilibrium part $\delta f_s$ combined symmetrically over parallel and perpendicular velocity directions and normalized to the equilibrium reference pressure. As the undifferentiated total, it is the parent abstraction for its directional decompositions; see [perturbed_pressure](name:perturbed_pressure) for the species-agnostic scalar concept.

The normalized total pressure moment is:

$$
\tilde{p}_s = \frac{1}{p_\mathrm{ref}} \int \frac{m_s}{3}\left(v_\parallel^2 + v_\perp^2\right) \delta f_s \, d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the species mass, $v_\parallel$ is the velocity component along the equilibrium magnetic field, $v_\perp^2 = v_{\perp 1}^2 + v_{\perp 2}^2$ is the squared perpendicular speed summed over the two gyrophase directions, and $p_\mathrm{ref} = n_\mathrm{ref} T_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference pressure. The factor $1/3$ imposes the isotropic trace average $\tilde{p}_s = (\tilde{p}_\parallel + 2\tilde{p}_\perp)/3$.

This moment is computed in local linear gyrokinetic solvers as part of the perturbed-moment hierarchy. Its perpendicular projection is the [perpendicular_normalized_perturbed_pressure](name:perpendicular_normalized_perturbed_pressure) and the parallel particle-frame component is [parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure](name:parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure); the corresponding gyrocenter-frame parent is [parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure](name:parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure). For linear eigenmodes the quantity is generally complex-valued, with phase set by the eigenmode normalization convention; reported magnitudes are normalization-dependent.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the velocity-space moment of the perturbed particle distribution yields a net pressure enhancement above the equilibrium reference pressure.

NAMES.name: normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1
NAMES.short: Dimensionless first-order Bessel-weighted total pressure moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution from a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, normalized to the equilibrium species pressure. It is the sum of the parallel and perpendicular J1-weighted pressure moments and encodes finite-Larmor-radius contributions to the gyrokinetic field response.
NAMES.long:
The normalized perturbed pressure Bessel-1 moment is the finite-Larmor-radius-weighted total pressure response carried by the perturbed gyrocenter distribution of a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode for a given species. The first-order Bessel factor $J_1$ selects the component of the pressure moment associated with the gyroaverage gradient in the perpendicular plane, so this moment vanishes in the long-wavelength limit and complements the $J_0$-weighted gyroaveraged pressure that survives there.

For species $s$ the dimensionless moment is the sum of its parallel and perpendicular parts, normalized to the equilibrium species pressure $p_s$:

$$
\widehat{P}^{(J_1)}_s = \widehat{P}^{(J_1)}_{\parallel s} + \widehat{P}^{(J_1)}_{\perp s} = \frac{1}{p_s}\int d^3v\, m_s\left(v_\parallel^2 + \frac{v_\perp^2}{2}\right) J_1(\lambda_s)\,\widetilde{F}_{g,s}
$$

where $p_s = n_s T_s$ is the equilibrium species pressure (in pascals), $m_s$ is the species mass (in kilograms), $v_\parallel$ and $v_\perp$ are the velocities parallel and perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field (in meters per second), $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element, and $\widetilde{F}_{g,s}$ is the complex eigenfunction amplitude of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution. The Bessel argument is $\lambda_s = k_\perp v_\perp/\Omega_s$, with $k_\perp$ the magnitude of the wave vector perpendicular to the equilibrium field (in inverse meters) and $\Omega_s = |q_s| B/m_s$ the positive cyclotron frequency magnitude (in inverse seconds). The result is dimensionless because the integral is divided by $p_s$.

In linear gyrokinetics the eigenmode is represented by complex amplitudes multiplying a harmonic dependence such as $\exp[i(\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{R}-\omega t)]$, and this moment inherits the same arbitrary global phase and amplitude normalization as $\widetilde{F}_{g,s}$. A common convention fixes a reference field amplitude, for example the electrostatic potential, to be real; changing that reference phase multiplies all eigenmode moments by the same complex factor, so only relative phases between moments and fields carry physical meaning.

Because the linear eigenmode amplitude is arbitrary, there is no universal absolute range; magnitudes are reported relative to whatever reference field amplitude the calculation adopts. At small $k_\perp$ the $J_1$-weighted moment is typically smaller than the corresponding unweighted or $J_0$-weighted pressure moment and grows toward them as $\lambda_s$ increases through order unity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the real part of the J1-weighted total pressure moment is in phase with the chosen real reference field amplitude, corresponding to an increase of the perturbed pressure relative to the equilibrium species pressure.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_normalized_perturbed_pressure
NAMES.short: Dimensionless perpendicular-pressure perturbation obtained from the perpendicular kinetic-energy moment of a perturbed distribution function for a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode. It is normalized by a reference equilibrium thermal pressure for the relevant particle population.
NAMES.long:
Perpendicular normalized perturbed pressure is the part of a pressure perturbation associated with particle kinetic energy perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field. In linear gyrokinetics it is a dimensionless eigenmode amplitude formed from the perpendicular second velocity moment of the perturbed distribution function and a chosen reference equilibrium thermal pressure.

For a particle population $s$, a common particle-space definition is:

$$
\tilde{p}_{\perp,s} = \frac{1}{p_\mathrm{ref}} \int \frac{1}{2} m_s v_\perp^2\,\delta f_s\,d^3v
$$

where $\tilde{p}_{\perp,s}$ is dimensionless, $m_s$ is the particle mass in kg, $v_\perp$ is the speed perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field in m s$^{-1}$, $\delta f_s$ is the perturbed distribution-function amplitude with units of density per velocity-space volume, $d^3v$ is a velocity-space volume element with units $(\mathrm{m\,s}^{-1})^3$, and $p_\mathrm{ref}$ is a reference pressure in Pa. The numerator therefore has pressure units; for example, $p_\mathrm{ref}$ may be an equilibrium species pressure such as $n_\mathrm{ref}T_\mathrm{ref}$ when $T_\mathrm{ref}$ is expressed as energy per particle.

This quantity is computed by taking the perpendicular kinetic-energy moment of the perturbed distribution function, or equivalently from evolved pressure moments in a gyrokinetic model. Together with the parallel pressure moment it describes pressure anisotropy in the perturbed distribution; for a gyrotropic perturbation, the scalar pressure perturbation is related to the parallel and perpendicular parts by $\tilde{p} = (\tilde{p}_\parallel + 2\tilde{p}_\perp)/3$.

There is no normalization-independent typical magnitude for a linear eigenmode amplitude, because the absolute eigenfunction scale is set by the chosen normalization. Within a fixed normalization, the value indicates the local perpendicular thermal-pressure response relative to the reference equilibrium pressure.

For complex linear eigenmodes, $\tilde{p}_\perp$ is generally a complex amplitude. Its phase is relative to the chosen eigenmode reference, so the sign of a real representation is not an independent physical convention; relative phases, ratios, and magnitudes within the same normalization carry the invariant information.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1
NAMES.short: Dimensionless perpendicular pressure moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution for a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, weighted by the first-order Bessel function J1 of the gyroaveraging argument. It is the Bessel-1 counterpart of the normalized perpendicular gyrocenter pressure perturbation.
NAMES.long:
The perpendicular normalized perturbed pressure Bessel-1 moment is the perpendicular kinetic-energy moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution weighted by $J_1$. It represents the finite-Larmor-radius part of the perpendicular pressure response of a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode and is generally a complex eigenfunction amplitude.

The normalized moment is defined by

$$
\hat{\delta p}_{\perp,J_1} = \frac{1}{n_\mathrm{ref} T_\mathrm{ref}} \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} \frac{m v_\perp^2}{2}\, J_1\!\left(k_\perp \rho(v_\perp)\right)\, \delta f_\mathrm{gc}(\mathbf{v})\, d^3v
$$

where $\hat{\delta p}_{\perp,J_1}$ is dimensionless, $n_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference density in $\mathrm{m}^{-3}$, and $T_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference particle energy so that $n_\mathrm{ref}T_\mathrm{ref}$ is a reference pressure. Here $m$ is the species mass in kg, $v_\perp$ is the speed perpendicular to the background magnetic field in $\mathrm{m\,s}^{-1}$, $J_1$ is the dimensionless first-order Bessel function, $k_\perp$ is the perpendicular wave-number magnitude in $\mathrm{m}^{-1}$, and $\rho(v_\perp)=v_\perp/|\Omega|$ is the velocity-dependent gyroradius in meters for cyclotron angular frequency $\Omega$ in $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$. The perturbed gyrocenter distribution $\delta f_\mathrm{gc}$ has units $\mathrm{s}^3\,\mathrm{m}^{-6}$, and the velocity-space measure $d^3v$ has units $\mathrm{m}^3\,\mathrm{s}^{-3}$; using velocity variables $(v_\parallel,v_\perp,\alpha)$, $d^3v = v_\perp\,dv_\perp\,d\alpha\,dv_\parallel$, with $v_\parallel$ the velocity along the background magnetic field and $\alpha$ the gyroangle.

This quantity is computed from the eigenmode distribution function by carrying out the velocity-space moment for each species and wave vector. It is not a directly measured thermodynamic pressure; experimental fluctuation measurements may constrain related density, temperature, or field perturbations, while this gyrocenter moment is obtained through gyrokinetic interpretation or simulation.

The $J_1$ weighting separates a finite-Larmor-radius contribution from the unweighted or $J_0$-gyroaveraged perpendicular pressure moments, linking it to related quantities such as [perpendicular_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure](name:perpendicular_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure) and perpendicular_normalized_gyrocenter_gyroaveraged_pressure. The complementary parallel contribution is [parallel_normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1](name:parallel_normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1), and their combination gives the corresponding total Bessel-1 pressure moment.

There is no normalization-independent typical magnitude for a linear eigenmode, because multiplying the eigenfunction by any nonzero complex constant rescales this moment. Values are therefore interpreted as relative complex amplitudes only after the eigenmode amplitude and phase have been fixed by the chosen normalization.
NAMES.sign: Positive when, after the eigenmode phase has been fixed by the selected reference perturbation, the Bessel-weighted excess of perpendicular gyrocenter kinetic energy in the defining velocity-space integral is positive.

NAMES.name: perturbed_vector_potential
NAMES.short: Perturbation of the electromagnetic vector potential associated with magnetic fluctuations in gyrokinetic turbulence. It denotes the vector-potential fluctuation as a physical field, not a specific component, projection, or normalization; normalized child quantities express this field after scaling by a reference electromagnetic quantity.
NAMES.long:
Perturbed vector potential is the fluctuating part $\delta\mathbf{A}$ of the electromagnetic vector potential associated with turbulence-scale magnetic perturbations. It is a vector quantity: it covers the full vector-potential perturbation and any explicitly defined component, projection, or normalized representation, without being limited to the parallel component or to a particular normalization.

The magnetic perturbation associated with a vector-potential perturbation is defined by its curl:

$$
\delta\mathbf{B} = \nabla \times \delta\mathbf{A}
$$

where $\delta\mathbf{B}$ is the fluctuating magnetic field and $\nabla\times$ is the spatial curl operator. The vector potential is gage dependent: adding the gradient of a scalar gage function to $\delta\mathbf{A}$ leaves $\delta\mathbf{B}$ unchanged, so comparisons of $\delta\mathbf{A}$ require a consistent gage and, when applicable, a stated normalization.

In gyrokinetic turbulence calculations, $\delta\mathbf{A}$ is obtained from the electromagnetic field equations coupled to particle or gyrocenter dynamics. Its parallel projection often controls magnetic-flutter transport across flux surfaces, while other components may be needed for a complete electromagnetic perturbation. Experimentally, it is usually inferred indirectly from magnetic-field fluctuation measurements or perturbative reconstruction rather than measured as an absolute potential.

The physical vector potential has dimensions of magnetic field times length. For magnetic fluctuations of $10^{-5}-10^{-2}$ T over perpendicular scales of $10^{-3}-10^{-1}$ m, representative unnormalized amplitudes are about $10^{-8}-10^{-3}$ T m. Normalized forms, such as [normalized perturbed vector potential](name:normalized_perturbed_vector_potential), are dimensionless and their numerical range depends on the reference electromagnetic scale.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the reported component of $\delta\mathbf{A}$ points along the positive direction of its explicitly stated basis; in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame this means $+\hat{R}$ for the radial component, $+\hat{\phi}$ in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, and $+\hat{Z}$ upward for the vertical component.

NAMES.name: normalized_perturbed_vector_potential
NAMES.short: Vector of the dimensionless perturbed electromagnetic vector potential in gyrokinetic turbulence, normalized by a reference electromagnetic scale, whose parallel projection drives magnetic-flutter transport across flux surfaces.
NAMES.long:
The normalized perturbed vector potential is the fluctuating electromagnetic vector potential $\delta\mathbf{A}$ in gyrokinetic plasma turbulence, rendered dimensionless by dividing by a reference scale $B_\text{ref} \rho_\text{ref}$, where $B_\text{ref}$ is a reference magnetic-field strength and $\rho_\text{ref}$ is a reference ion gyroradius. In tokamak geometry the dominant electromagnetic degree of freedom is the component aligned with the equilibrium field $\hat{b}$, which enters the gyrocenter equations of motion through the parallel canonical momentum $p_\parallel - q_s \delta A_\parallel / c$, where $q_s$ is the species charge and $c$ is the speed of light (Gaussian units).

The normalized parallel projection $\tilde{A}_\parallel$ is determined self-consistently by the gyrokinetic parallel Ampère equation:

$$
-\nabla_\perp^2 \tilde{A}_\parallel = \frac{\beta_\text{ref}}{2} \sum_s q_s \int v_\parallel \tilde{f}_s \, d^3v
$$

where $\beta_\text{ref}$ is the reference plasma beta, $v_\parallel$ is the particle velocity component parallel to $\hat{b}$, and $\tilde{f}_s$ is the normalized perturbed distribution function.

The child [parallel_normalized_perturbed_vector_potential](name:parallel_normalized_perturbed_vector_potential) provides the scalar parallel projection and directly governs the magnetic-flutter energy transport quantified by [normalized_energy_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential](name:normalized_energy_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential) and the momentum transport described by [momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential](name:momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential). This normalized vector is the dimensionless counterpart of the dimensional [perturbed_vector_potential](name:perturbed_vector_potential).
NAMES.sign: Positive when $\delta A_\parallel$ is aligned with the equilibrium magnetic field direction $\hat{b}$, i.e., in the direction of increasing arc length along the field line.

NAMES.name: parallel_normalized_perturbed_vector_potential
NAMES.short: Dimensionless gyrokinetic perturbation formed from the component of the vector-potential fluctuation parallel to the equilibrium magnetic field, normalized by a reference vector-potential scale. Its signed or complex value depends on the chosen electromagnetic gage and, for linear eigenmodes, on the arbitrary eigenfunction phase.
NAMES.long:
Parallel normalized perturbed vector potential is the dimensionless electromagnetic gyrokinetic field obtained by projecting the vector-potential fluctuation along the equilibrium magnetic field and dividing by a reference vector-potential scale. It represents the shear-Alfvén part of the perturbation that enters parallel particle dynamics and magnetic-flutter coupling, but the vector potential itself is not gage invariant.

The normalized field is defined by

$$
\widehat{A}_\parallel = \frac{\delta A_\parallel}{A_{\parallel,\mathrm{ref}}}, \qquad \delta A_\parallel = \delta\mathbf{A}\cdot\mathbf{b}
$$

where $\delta\mathbf{A}$ is the vector-potential perturbation, $\mathbf{b}$ is the unit vector along the equilibrium magnetic field, $\delta A_\parallel$ and $A_{\parallel,\mathrm{ref}}$ have physical units tesla meter, equivalently Wb m$^{-1}$, and $\widehat{A}_\parallel$ is dimensionless. The reference scale is the one used consistently for the accompanying gyrokinetic variables; a common choice is $A_{\parallel,\mathrm{ref}}=T_\mathrm{ref}/(q_\mathrm{ref}v_\mathrm{ref})$, with $T_\mathrm{ref}$ an energy, $q_\mathrm{ref}$ a charge, and $v_\mathrm{ref}$ a speed.

In gyrokinetic calculations this quantity is usually solved together with the perturbed electrostatic potential and distribution functions. The physical parallel vector potential is constrained by the parallel component of Ampere's law; in a Fourier representation and when displacement current is neglected, it is commonly related to the parallel current perturbation by $k_\perp^2\delta A_\parallel \approx \mu_0\delta j_\parallel$, with the overall algebraic sign set by the Fourier phase convention and with possible corrections from electron inertia or skin-depth effects. Experimentally it is not measured directly; it may be inferred indirectly from magnetic-fluctuation diagnostics or from model-based reconstruction of electromagnetic turbulence.

The value is gage dependent because an electromagnetic gage transformation changes $\delta\mathbf{A}$ while leaving the observable fields unchanged. Physical comparisons should therefore use a specified gage or gage-invariant combinations such as the resulting magnetic perturbation or electromagnetic fields. For linear eigenmodes, the whole eigenfunction can also be multiplied by an arbitrary complex phase, so real and imaginary parts are phase dependent whereas amplitudes and phase-invariant ratios are more directly comparable.

There is no universal typical numerical range for this normalized quantity. Linear calculations often choose an arbitrary eigenfunction normalization, and nonlinear values depend on the reference scale, gage, plasma beta, fluctuation level, and mode spectrum; values should be compared only within a consistent normalization and gage convention.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the chosen real representative of $\delta A_\parallel$ points along the equilibrium magnetic field direction after the electromagnetic gage and any linear-eigenfunction phase have been fixed.

NAMES.name: parallel_normalized_perturbed_vector_potential_amplitude
NAMES.short: Modulus of the complex normalized perturbed parallel vector potential eigenfunction for a gyrokinetic mode. It quantifies the dimensionless electromagnetic fluctuation amplitude associated with field-aligned current and magnetic flutter.
NAMES.long:
Parallel normalized perturbed vector potential amplitude is the non-negative modulus of the complex dimensionless perturbation $\delta \tilde{A}_\parallel$, where the parallel component is taken along the local equilibrium magnetic field. It characterizes the electromagnetic part of a gyrokinetic fluctuation and vanishes for a purely electrostatic perturbation.

For a complex normalized eigenfunction $\delta \tilde{A}_\parallel = \delta A_\parallel/A_\mathrm{ref}$, the amplitude is defined by:

$$
|\delta \tilde{A}_\parallel| = \left|\frac{\delta A_\parallel}{A_\mathrm{ref}}\right| = \sqrt{\left(\Re\,\delta \tilde{A}_\parallel\right)^2 + \left(\Im\,\delta \tilde{A}_\parallel\right)^2}
$$

where $\delta A_\parallel$ is the physical perturbed parallel vector potential with units of T m, $A_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference vector-potential scale with the same units, and $\delta \tilde{A}_\parallel$ is dimensionless. The exact reference scale is set by the gyrokinetic normalization; common choices include a magnetic scale such as $\rho_\mathrm{ref} B_\mathrm{ref}$, with $\rho_\mathrm{ref}$ in meters and $B_\mathrm{ref}$ in tesla, or an equivalent potential-based scale specified by the chosen nondimensionalization.

In gyrokinetic modeling, $\delta A_\parallel$ is computed from the electromagnetic field solve and is constrained by parallel Ampere's law. In Fourier representation, this relates $k_\perp^2 \delta A_\parallel$ to the perturbed parallel-current moment, for example $\mu_0 \sum_s q_s \int v_\parallel g_s\,d^3v$, where $k_\perp$ is the perpendicular wavenumber in m^-1, $q_s$ is species charge, $v_\parallel$ is parallel velocity, and $g_s$ is the non-adiabatic distribution perturbation. For linear eigenmodes the overall complex scale may be arbitrary, so this amplitude is most meaningful together with the stated eigenmode normalization, relative variation, or ratios to other fluctuating fields.

Typical dimensionless amplitudes are strongly normalization dependent. With equilibrium-scale normalizations, electrostatic drift-wave cases are often near 0, weakly electromagnetic microturbulence commonly gives about 1e-6-1e-3, and kinetic-ballooning or shear-Alfvenic cases can reach 1e-3-1; eigenfunctions rescaled to unit maximum can have peak amplitude of order 1 by construction.

NAMES.name: parallel_normalized_perturbed_vector_potential_real_part
NAMES.short: Real component of the complex normalized perturbed vector potential parallel to the equilibrium magnetic field, expressed versus field-line poloidal angle in a gyrokinetic eigenmode. It depends on the selected gage, reference vector-potential scale, and arbitrary complex eigenfunction phase.
NAMES.long:
Parallel normalized perturbed vector potential real part is the real component of the complex eigenfunction representing the perturbation of the vector potential projected along the equilibrium magnetic-field direction. It describes the electromagnetic perturbation associated with parallel electric-field and magnetic-flutter dynamics after a gage and complex phase have been fixed. The quantity is dimensionless because the physical vector potential is divided by a real, positive reference vector-potential scale.

The real component is defined from the complex normalized eigenfunction by

$$
a_{\parallel,R}(\theta) = \operatorname{Re}\!\left[\frac{\delta A_\parallel(\theta)}{A_{\parallel,\mathrm{ref}}}\right]
$$

where $\delta A_\parallel$ is the complex perturbed vector potential parallel to the equilibrium magnetic field in T m, $A_{\parallel,\mathrm{ref}}$ is a real positive reference vector-potential scale in T m, $\theta$ is the field-line poloidal angle in radians, and $a_{\parallel,R}$ is dimensionless. A reproducible normalization should state the physical scale used for $A_{\parallel,\mathrm{ref}}$; a common gyrokinetic choice is $B_\mathrm{ref}\rho_\mathrm{ref}$, with $B_\mathrm{ref}$ a reference magnetic-field magnitude in tesla and $\rho_\mathrm{ref}$ a reference gyroradius in meters.

In linear gyrokinetic calculations, $\delta A_\parallel$ is obtained as part of a complex eigenmode, so its overall amplitude and phase are arbitrary until an eigenfunction normalization and phase convention are imposed. The electromagnetic gage must also be specified, because the parallel vector potential is gage dependent. Together with parallel_normalized_perturbed_vector_potential_imaginary_part, this quantity forms the complex normalized field [parallel_normalized_perturbed_vector_potential](name:parallel_normalized_perturbed_vector_potential_amplitude) through $a_\parallel=a_{\parallel,R}+i a_{\parallel,I}$; a normalized modulus would be $|a_\parallel|=(a_{\parallel,R}^2+a_{\parallel,I}^2)^{1/2}$ and is not the same as this signed real component.

No universal physical range exists for a linear eigenfunction, because its amplitude can be rescaled without changing the mode structure. With a peak-modulus convention such as $\max_\theta |a_\parallel|=1$, values of the real part usually lie between -1 and 1; with an RMS convention, the RMS value is order 1 by construction. Values from different calculations are directly comparable only when the same gage, normalization scale, amplitude normalization, and phase convention are used.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the perturbed vector potential is projected along the positive equilibrium magnetic-field direction and its normalized complex value lies in the positive real direction after applying the stated gage, real positive normalization scale, and eigenfunction phase convention.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_particle_temperature_to_reference_particle_temperature
NAMES.short: Dimensionless ratio of a particle species temperature to a normalization reference temperature, setting the relative thermal speed of that species in a gyrokinetic simulation.
NAMES.long:
The ratio of a particle species temperature $T_s$ to a reference temperature $T_{\rm ref}$ is a fundamental dimensionless input in gyrokinetic flux-tube simulations, governing the amplitude of thermal fluctuations and the relative equilibrium distribution widths between co-existing plasma species.

The defining relation is:

$$
\tau_s = \frac{T_s}{T_{\rm ref}}
$$

where $T_s$ is the temperature of species $s$ and $T_{\rm ref}$ is the global normalization reference temperature, often chosen as the electron temperature at the outboard midplane flux surface. Through the thermal speed $v_{T,s} = \sqrt{T_s / m_s}$, where $m_s$ is the species mass, $\tau_s$ directly sets the gyrokinetic Maxwellian width and controls interspecies temperature contrasts that drive ion-temperature-gradient and trapped-electron-mode instabilities.

This quantity is equivalent to [normalized_particle_temperature](name:ratio_of_particle_temperature_to_reference_particle_temperature) and overlaps with the more generic [normalized_temperature](name:ratio_of_particle_temperature_to_reference_particle_temperature); it is the temperature analog of [ratio_of_particle_number_density_to_reference_number_density](name:ratio_of_particle_number_density_to_reference_number_density). In practice it is prescribed as a species-level input parameter to a gyrokinetic code, derived from experimental profiles or equilibrium reconstruction at the chosen flux surface.

Typical values in core-plasma flux-tube runs span $\tau_s \approx 0.1$–10, with the reference species by definition having $\tau_s = 1$ and minority or impurity species taking values determined by their experimental temperature ratios.

NAMES.name: toroidal_reference_magnetic_field
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the equilibrium magnetic field evaluated at the reference major radius in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame. It is a signed field component, distinct from the corresponding vacuum toroidal field.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal reference magnetic field is the toroidal component of the equilibrium magnetic field evaluated at the chosen reference location whose major radius is $R_\mathrm{ref}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is a signed component of the equilibrium field and is distinct from both the full magnetic-field magnitude and the vacuum toroidal-field estimate.

The defining projection at the reference point is:

$$
B_\mathrm{ref} = \mathbf{B}_\mathrm{eq}(R_\mathrm{ref}, \phi, Z_\mathrm{ref}) \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{eq}$ is the equilibrium magnetic field, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector, $B_\mathrm{ref}$ and the component $B_\phi$ are in tesla, and $R_\mathrm{ref}$ and $Z_\mathrm{ref}$ are in meters. In an axisymmetric equilibrium the value is independent of $\phi$; if the reference is specified only by major radius, $Z_\mathrm{ref}$ denotes the associated vertical coordinate of that reference location.

The value is computed by evaluating the equilibrium field at the reference point and projecting onto $\hat{\phi}$. It is the reference-location specialization of [toroidal_magnetic_field](name:toroidal_magnetic_field); [toroidal_magnetic_field_at_magnetic_axis](name:toroidal_magnetic_field_at_magnetic_axis) uses the magnetic-axis location instead. The related [toroidal_vacuum_magnetic_field](name:toroidal_vacuum_magnetic_field) is often written $B_\mathrm{vac}=F_\mathrm{vac}/R_\mathrm{ref}$, where $F_\mathrm{vac}$ is in T m and $B_\mathrm{vac}$ is in T, or equivalently $B_\mathrm{vac}=B_{\phi0}R_0/R_\mathrm{ref}$, where $B_{\phi0}$ is in T and $R_0$ is in meters. The equilibrium reference value can differ from this vacuum value because plasma pressure and current modify the toroidal-field function and because the reference point may be displaced by plasma shaping or Shafranov shift.

Typical magnitudes are 1-6 T in medium-sized to large tokamaks, below 1 T in some low-field spherical tokamaks, and up to about 8-12 T in high-field devices. Quantities such as gyrofrequency scales or gyroradii normally use $|B_\mathrm{ref}|$ or a full-field magnitude; the signed value is retained when toroidal-field orientation matters.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $B_\phi$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: normalized_particle_density
NAMES.short: Dimensionless ratio of a particle species number density to a chosen reference number density.
NAMES.long:
Normalized particle density is the number density of a specified particle species divided by a reference number density used to nondimensionalize the system. It preserves the relative abundance of each species while removing the physical density unit.

The defining ratio is:

$$
n_{s,\mathrm{norm}} = \frac{n_s}{n_\mathrm{ref}}
$$

where $n_s$ is the particle number density of species $s$ in m$^{-3}$ and $n_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference number density in m$^{-3}$; the result is dimensionless.

In gyrokinetic and turbulence calculations, $n_s$ is usually taken from the equilibrium or background density at the simulated location, while $n_\mathrm{ref}$ is a common normalization density shared by all species. With a common reference density, the set of normalized densities provides the charge-weighted equilibrium density balance, such as inline $\sum_s Z_s n_{s,\mathrm{norm}} = 0$ for signed charge number $Z_s$ when all relevant species are included. This balance is a normalization and background quasineutrality condition, not the complete gyrokinetic quasineutrality relation for fluctuations and fields.

Physically allowed values are non-negative, with no fixed upper bound. Typical values are 0.1-3 for bulk electrons and main ions when the reference density is close to the plasma density, 10$^{-6}$-10$^{-2}$ for trace impurities, and 10$^{-3}$-1 for minority or non-trace impurity species depending on composition and normalization choice.

NAMES.name: perturbed_particle_pressure
NAMES.short: Abstract parent for the normalized gyrotropic pressure-tensor moment of the perturbed particle distribution in gyrokinetic turbulence, encompassing the parallel and perpendicular components of the pressure decomposition.
NAMES.long:
This parent quantity represents the dimensionless pressure perturbation carried by the particle distribution function $\delta f_s$ for a given species in linear gyrokinetic eigenmode analysis. The full pressure tensor of the perturbed distribution is gyrotropic, decomposing into two independent scalar components along and perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$. Normalization by a reference thermal pressure $p_{\rm ref} = n_{\rm ref} T_{\rm ref}$ makes the moment dimensionless and enables direct comparison across species and plasma parameters.

The defining kinetic moment is:

$$
\delta \hat{p}_s = \frac{1}{n_{\rm ref} T_{\rm ref}} \int m_s v^2 \, \delta f_s \, d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the species mass, $v$ is the particle speed, $n_{\rm ref}$ is a reference number density, and $T_{\rm ref}$ is a reference temperature. The directional decomposition into parallel and perpendicular gyrotropic components is carried by [normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure](name:normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure). The analogous gyrocenter quantity [normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure](name:normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure) differs from the particle moment by finite-Larmor-radius corrections that become significant when the perturbation wavelength is comparable to the thermal gyroradius. For a linear eigenmode, the complex phase of $\delta f_s$ is arbitrary; only relative amplitudes between moments evaluated at the same wavevector carry physical meaning.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the perturbation corresponds to a local enhancement of particle pressure above the equilibrium background value.

NAMES.name: normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure
NAMES.short: Normalized gyrotropic pressure-tensor moment of the perturbed particle distribution for a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, decomposed into components parallel and perpendicular to the background magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
The normalized particle perturbed pressure is a gyrotropic vector quantity representing the pressure fluctuation of the physical particle population in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, decomposed into components parallel and perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$, each expressed dimensionlessly as a ratio to a reference thermal pressure $p_\mathrm{ref}$.

For species $s$, the parallel and perpendicular components are the second velocity-space moments of the perturbed particle distribution function $\delta f_s$:

$$
\hat{p}_{\parallel,s} = \frac{m_s}{p_\mathrm{ref}} \int v_\parallel^2 \, \delta f_s \, d^3v, \qquad \hat{p}_{\perp,s} = \frac{m_s}{2 \, p_\mathrm{ref}} \int v_\perp^2 \, \delta f_s \, d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the species mass, $v_\parallel$ and $v_\perp$ are velocities parallel and perpendicular to $\mathbf{B}$, and $p_\mathrm{ref} = n_\mathrm{ref} T_\mathrm{ref}$ is evaluated at the outboard midplane.

Unlike the corresponding [gyroaveraged gyrocenter perturbed pressure], this quantity is built from the full particle distribution function, implicitly incorporating finite-Larmor-radius corrections through the particle-to-gyrocenter coordinate transformation. The isotropic scalar parent particle_perturbed_pressure is recovered as the trace average $\hat{p}_s = (\hat{p}_{\parallel,s} + 2\hat{p}_{\perp,s})/3$. The [parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure](name:parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure) and [perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure](name:perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure) components together encode the pressure anisotropy of the eigenmode, with the ratio $\hat{p}_{\parallel,s}/\hat{p}_{\perp,s}$ quantifying deviation from local thermodynamic equilibrium relevant to mirror-mode and fire-hose stability.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the species pressure perturbation corresponds to a local increase above the equilibrium background pressure.

NAMES.name: parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure
NAMES.short: Normalized parallel pressure moment of the perturbed particle distribution function for a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode. It is the complex parallel component of the particle pressure perturbation, normalized to a reference pressure, and is distinct from the corresponding gyrocenter moment.
NAMES.long:
The parallel normalized particle perturbed pressure is a dimensionless complex eigenmode moment of the perturbed particle distribution function. It represents the fluctuation of the pressure associated with random particle motion along the local magnetic-field direction, evaluated in particle variables rather than gyrocenter variables.

For species $s$, using reference density $n_{\mathrm{ref},s}$ and reference temperature $T_{\mathrm{ref},s}$ expressed as an energy, a common normalization is

$$
\widehat{p}_{\parallel s}^{\,\mathrm{part}} = \frac{m_s}{n_{\mathrm{ref},s} T_{\mathrm{ref},s}} \int v_\parallel^2\,\delta f_s^{\,\mathrm{part}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the particle mass, $v_\parallel$ is the particle velocity component along the magnetic field in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $\delta f_s^{\,\mathrm{part}}$ is the perturbed particle distribution function in $\mathrm{m^{-6}\,s^3}$, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element in $\mathrm{m^3\,s^{-3}}$. The denominator $n_{\mathrm{ref},s}T_{\mathrm{ref},s}$ is a reference pressure; if temperature is supplied in eV it must be converted to joules for this expression.

In linear gyrokinetic analysis this moment is computed by applying the parallel-pressure velocity-space weight to the particle perturbed distribution eigenfunction and integrating over velocity space. When the same reference pressure and particle distribution are used, the scalar normalized perturbed pressure is related to the gyrotropic components by $\widehat{p}_s^{\mathrm{part}}=(\widehat{p}_{\parallel s}^{\mathrm{part}}+2\widehat{p}_{\perp s}^{\mathrm{part}})/3$; this trace relation does not specify nongyrotropic or off-diagonal pressure-tensor moments. The particle moment should not be assumed equal to the gyrocenter parallel pressure moment, because the variables used in the velocity-space moment are different.

Typical magnitudes are normalization dependent. With unit-amplitude eigenfunction normalizations, values from about $10^{-3}$ to $10$ are common, while ratios between species, radial locations, or pressure components and the relative complex phase usually carry more physical meaning than the absolute magnitude.

For a linear eigenmode the overall complex amplitude and phase are arbitrary. A self-contained convention is obtained by choosing one reference eigenfunction component to be real with a fixed positive value; changing that choice multiplies all complex moments by the same complex constant, leaving relative phases and normalized ratios invariant.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure
NAMES.short: Dimensionless perpendicular-pressure moment of the perturbed particle distribution of a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, normalized by a reference thermal pressure. It is the second velocity-space moment in perpendicular kinetic energy of the perturbed distribution rather than an independent thermodynamic pressure.
NAMES.long:
Perpendicular normalized particle perturbed pressure is the dimensionless perpendicular-pressure moment of the perturbed particle distribution function for a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode. It measures the fluctuating perpendicular thermal energy density carried by the perturbed distribution, expressed in particle (laboratory) velocity variables and scaled by a reference thermal pressure. It is a velocity-space moment of the perturbation, not an independent thermodynamic state variable.

For species $s$, the normalized perpendicular pressure moment is

$$
\delta \hat{p}^{\mathrm{particle}}_{\perp s} = \frac{1}{n_{\mathrm{ref}} T_{\mathrm{ref}}} \int \frac{m_s v_\perp^2}{2}\, \delta f^{\mathrm{particle}}_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\, d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the particle mass in kg, $v_\perp$ is the speed perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field in m s$^{-1}$, $\delta f^{\mathrm{particle}}_s$ is the perturbed particle distribution in units m$^{-3}$ (m s$^{-1}$)$^{-3}$, and the velocity-space element $d^3v$ has units (m s$^{-1}$)$^3$. The reference density $n_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is in m$^{-3}$ and the reference temperature $T_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is an energy per particle in J; a temperature given in eV must be multiplied by the elementary charge before forming the reference pressure $n_{\mathrm{ref}} T_{\mathrm{ref}}$.

The perpendicular and parallel particle pressure moments combine into the total particle pressure moment of the eigenmode. With the perpendicular component counting the two degrees of freedom orthogonal to $\mathbf{B}$ and the parallel component the single field-aligned degree of freedom, the trace-weighted combination $\delta \hat{p}^{\mathrm{particle}}_s = (2\,\delta \hat{p}^{\mathrm{particle}}_{\perp s} + \delta \hat{p}^{\mathrm{particle}}_{\parallel s})/3$ recovers normalized_total_perturbed_particle_pressure_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode, where $\delta \hat{p}^{\mathrm{particle}}_{\parallel s}$ is [parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure](name:parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure). The difference between this particle-frame moment and its gyrocenter counterpart [perpendicular_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure](name:perpendicular_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure) reflects the coordinate transformation between particle and gyrocenter velocity variables.

The moment is obtained by integrating the eigenmode perturbed distribution over velocity space in particle variables; the reference density and temperature defining the normalization are part of the prescribed normalization convention of the calculation. Because a linear eigenmode has an arbitrary overall amplitude, no absolute magnitude range is meaningful: the quantity scales with the chosen eigenfunction normalization and is generally complex.

The complex value carries both magnitude and phase relative to the arbitrary global phase of the eigenmode, which is itself set by the eigenfunction normalization convention. Only relative magnitudes and phase differences between moments of the same eigenmode are physically meaningful; the sign of the real part by itself is not an invariant quantity.

NAMES.name: radial_derivative_of_elongation_of_flux_surface
NAMES.short: Radial rate of change of the flux surface elongation kappa with respect to normalized minor radius, measuring how rapidly the poloidal cross-section aspect ratio varies across nested flux surfaces.
NAMES.long:
The radial derivative of flux surface elongation quantifies how the vertical-to-horizontal shape of nested toroidal magnetic surfaces changes as a function of radial position. The flux surface elongation $\kappa$ equals the ratio of the vertical to horizontal semi-axis of the poloidal cross-section, so its radial derivative captures the rate at which flux surfaces become more (or less) vertically elongated moving outward from the magnetic axis.

The quantity is defined as:

$$
\frac{d\kappa}{d\hat{r}}
$$

where $\kappa$ is the [elongation of the flux surface](name:elongation_of_flux_surface) and $\hat{r}$ is the normalized minor radius running from 0 at the magnetic axis to 1 at the plasma boundary. Both $\kappa$ and $\hat{r}$ are dimensionless, so the derivative is also dimensionless.

This derivative is a required geometric input to local gyrokinetic flux-tube simulations, entering the metric coefficients that govern field-line curvature and grad-$B$ drift terms within the flux-tube domain. It belongs to the broader family of radial flux surface shape coefficient derivatives that also includes the [radial derivative of flux surface shape coefficient](name:radial_derivative_of_elongation_of_flux_surface). In plasmas with significant edge shaping, this quantity grows in magnitude toward the separatrix, while remaining near zero for nearly circular flux surfaces where $\kappa \approx 1$ throughout the minor radius.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the elongation $\kappa$ increases with increasing normalized minor radius $\hat{r}$, corresponding to flux surfaces that become more vertically elongated toward the plasma boundary.
